# Cyrus full plan: separation, bridge, portals, infra, one-session updates (2026-10-11)
Companion to CYRUS-TRACKER.md (state) and MASTER-PLAN.md (engine). Estimates are my judgement, not measurements.

## 0. Target architecture (what "done" looks like)
```
 cyrus.my (landing, Cloudflare)      app.cyrus.my  (Cyrus customer app)      admin.cyrus.my (Cyrus admin)
                          \               |                    /
                           +---- Cyrus services: API (api.cyrus.my) + workers + own DB + object storage/CDN + build service
                                          |  ^
                    Cyrus -> Nxeon:       |  |   Nxeon -> Cyrus:
                    Nxeon Platform API    |  |   Cyrus API v1 + signed webhooks
                    (identity, wallet,    v  |   (projects, builds, mods, entitlements)
                     servers, files)   nxeon.cloud (portal, billing, game servers, admin)
```
Principles: (1) Nxeon = identity + money + game-server hosting; Cyrus = everything about mods. (2) One account, one wallet, one Stripe. (3) The browser talks straight to the service that owns the feature; no relaying. (4) Every cross-app call is a versioned, tested contract. (5) Nothing in Nxeon breaks at any step: each phase is flag-gated and reversible.

## 1. Decisions to lock first (my recommendation in bold)
1. Repo shape: **one monorepo, several deployables** (`apps/nxeon`, `apps/cyrus`, `apps/cyrus-admin`, `apps/cyrus-site`, `packages/*` shared). One Claude session edits one repo and ships only what changed. Separate repos would make "one update applies everywhere" a cross-repo chore.
2. Payment: **Nxeon wallet/Stripe is the only money system** (already the coded default). Cyrus sells nothing itself; it asks Nxeon to charge.
3. Identity: **Nxeon is the identity provider**; cyrus.my accounts are lazily provisioned Nxeon accounts. "Sign in with Cyrus" on Nxeon is a button that lands on the same account.
4. Server access: **per-server, scoped grants** (section 3.3), never SSH credentials.
5. Hosting for Cyrus services: own VPS/dedicated pair (app + build/worker) behind Cloudflare; **separate Postgres** from Nxeon. Region chosen deliberately (primary is Singapore, node-2 Germany).
6. Admin: **Cyrus has its own admin; Nxeon admin shows a read-only Cyrus summary + deep link**; staff identity and roles come from Nxeon rbac.
7. Terms: separate Cyrus ToS/Privacy (with the library licence grant), reviewed by a lawyer before public launch.

## 2. Phases (order matters; each ends in something shippable)
**P0 Today, 1-2 h owner time: decisions + reviews.** Lock section 1; review the landing page when ready; skim v2/v3/v4/v5 mockups (they gate UI polish, not the backbone).
**P1 Front door (today).** Landing page review, then publish it as the cyrus.my static site (swap into /var/www/cyrus.my). Dual-host shell + SSO + purchase->credit (agent r36 running). Cert watcher finishes TLS when Cloudflare activates the zone.
**P2 Cloudflare for Nxeon (today/tomorrow, needs a zone token).** Restore real client IP (CF-Connecting-IP) in nginx + app first; proxy one hostname, then portal/site; keep game, mail and non-HTTP records grey; cache static only; websocket keepalive; Full (strict); measure US load time before/after.
**P3 Extract the Cyrus app (1-2 days of agent work).** Monorepo scaffold; `apps/cyrus` as its own Next app (own layout, own session cookie, own routes: dashboard, studios, library, mods, plans); move `components/cyrus`, `lib/cyrus`, `app/**/cyrus*` into packages/app; the 5 remaining baseline imports and the 185 app/component imports of Nxeon code are replaced by the host seam or shared packages (`packages/ui` for primitives, `packages/auth-client`, `packages/nxeon-client`, `packages/cyrus-client`); the Nxeon portal's Cyrus tab becomes thin (list, status, deep links, embed-free). Both still deploy from one place at first.
**P4 Bridge hardening (1-2 days, parallel with P3 where files differ).** Section 3 in full: Nxeon Platform API for servers/files with scoped grants, entitlement sync, webhooks live in the product, notifications, support context, server-aware Cyrus UX.
**P5 Data split (half a day + careful cutover).** Cyrus tables to their own database (28 tables, no FKs, user ids are plain strings; Nxeon-table access already gone via `cyrusDb`); dual-write or dump/restore with a short write freeze; rollback = repoint. Own backups from day one.
**P6 Portals (2-3 days, parallel agents).** Section 4 (customer) and section 5 (admin).
**P7 Infra move (1 day + soak).** New servers, Cloudflare in front, R2/CDN for packs and library, build service wiring, staging env, monitoring, backups, status page, deploy script with health-checked cutover and rollback (`promote-cyrus.sh`, same safety rules as promote-production.sh).
**P8 Launch gate (owner-gated).** Real-client test day, paid eval baseline + fix loop, API key replaces subscription login, legal, migrations/runbook (docs/CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK.md + CYRUS-MOVE-RUNBOOK.md), then flag order with the launch-pair guard.
Realistic today: P0, P1, start P2 (needs token), kick off P3 scaffolding. P3-P7 are multi-day even with parallel agents; the build lock on node-2 and your usage are the limits, not ideas.

## 3. The bridge, in detail
### 3.1 Identity and account lifecycle
Stable subject id (Nxeon user id) everywhere; never match on email. Sign in with Nxeon on cyrus.my (OIDC-style redirect, state/nonce, signed assertion, own session cookie); "Sign in with Cyrus" on Nxeon goes to the same account. First visit provisions the Cyrus profile silently (no second signup). Gaps to cover: verified email required; MFA lives at Nxeon; per-host sessions + back-channel logout; account suspend/ban propagation both ways (Cyrus-only abuse flags a user at Nxeon); deletion + data export cascade (GDPR) across both; Cyrus ToS acceptance recorded per user with version; admin view-as across hosts without leaking; account merge when someone already has two identities.
### 3.2 Money, plans, tokens
Plans (Katara, Saka, Yakko) and token packs are products in Nxeon billing; entitlement is Nxeon's, mirrored into Cyrus by webhook + short-TTL cache, **fail closed** when unknown. Purchases started on either site go through Nxeon checkout; credit to Cyrus tokens is idempotent (outbox, retries, daily reconciliation, honest pending/failed states); refunds and chargebacks reverse credits; invoices/VAT stay in Nxeon. Gaps: Creator Partner Program attribution for Cyrus plans (50% first / 10% recurring exists at Nxeon: decide if it applies); promo codes; free-tier grants and abuse limits; spend caps per user and global (AI cost vs revenue dashboard); tax/VAT decision still open.
### 3.3 Connecting servers ("install straight onto my servers")
Connect = a consent screen at Nxeon listing exactly what Cyrus may do, per server the user ticks. Scopes: `servers.read` (id, name, game, version/loader, status, RAM/CPU, player count), `inventory.read` (installed plugins/mods with versions: feeds the conflict engine before every build/install), `files.write.mods` (only mods/plugins/config/datapack/resource-pack paths, with hash preconditions), `server.reload` / `server.restart` (budgeted), `logs.read.tail` (for Server Doctor, health, post-install checks), `pack.set` (resource-pack URL + hash). Cyrus keeps the delivery orchestrator (journal, rollback); Nxeon exposes safe primitives and audits every call. Revocable any time; every call tied to user + server + grant; rate limited; idempotent. Webhooks Nxeon -> Cyrus: `server.version_changed` (mark mods outdated), `server.deleted`, `server.restarted`, `grant.revoked`. Users without Nxeon servers: download jar, "Try it" throwaway server, install guide. Pull to improve results: target version from the server, RAM-aware warnings (worldgen, creatures), existing-plugin conflicts, "Create a mod for this server" button on every Nxeon server page that prefills Cyrus.
### 3.4 Cross-product experience
Shared header package (account menu, balance, notifications, product switcher); deep links with silent SSO; one notification system (build finished, install result, mod outdated, takedown) with one preference center, email through Nxeon's mail stack from a cyrus.my sender (SPF/DKIM/DMARC for the new domain); support: tickets stay in Nxeon, carry Cyrus context (build id, spec, flight record), support can view-as; unified status page; cross-domain analytics/attribution (Meta/Google conversions, referral cookies) and a cookie-consent banner; SEO: `/mods/cyrus` redirect strategy to cyrus.my.

## 4. Cyrus customer app (app.cyrus.my): what it needs
Dashboard (projects, recent builds, mods, plan + tokens, connected servers, library contributions, activity); project page (revisions, builds with Test Flight status, install/rollback, configs, studios: texture, sound, model, motion, designers, config); new-mod flow with game/version/server pickers and cost shown first; library browser; mod pages (public, pass-rate badges, ratings); account (profile, connected Nxeon account + servers + grants, personal Cyrus API keys, notification prefs, data export/delete); plans/tokens (buy via Nxeon); onboarding tour and templates gallery; docs/help; changelog (customer-facing only); teams/shared projects (later, a real gap); referral/creator pages.
## 5. Admin portal (admin.cyrus.my, staff via Nxeon roles)
Overview (queue depth, build success rate, spend vs revenue, errors); builds (search, logs, rerun, kill, cost); users (lookup, plan/tokens adjust with audit, view-as, ban/suspend, GDPR tools); library moderation (hold queue, takedown/DMCA log, near-duplicate tools, trademark/real-weapon lists); flags and kill switches (launch-pair guard, AI gateway kill, global build pause, per-feature off); evals and pass-rates (run, compare, publish); capacity (build VM, node-2 flights, meshgen jobs, storage); cost governance (per-model spend, per-user caps, alerts); audit log; announcements; reconciliation view (Nxeon wallet vs Cyrus tokens, webhook failures, replay). Nxeon admin gets a read-only Cyrus card + deep link.

## 6. Cloudflare and infrastructure
cyrus.my zone (pending): apex + www (landing static), app, api, admin, cdn/packs (R2) subdomains; WAF + rate limits, Turnstile on sign-up and "Create Mod", bot protection; Full (strict) with origin certs; static cache rules; pack and library delivery from R2/CDN with signed URLs (sound library only when cleared). Nxeon zones per P2 (client IP first, game and mail records stay grey). Own Postgres + PgBouncer, nightly encrypted backups off-box, second copy of the proprietary SFX library (tank is one disk with no redundancy). Staging environment; observability (logs, metrics, uptime, error tracking, per-build cost telemetry); status page; secrets in one place; **the build service must move from subscription login to an API key before any public launch** with hard spend caps; build-queue fairness and capacity plan beyond the single build VM.

## 7. One Claude session updates everything
Monorepo layout above. `scripts/ship <target|all>` detects what changed (apps and packages graph), runs tests + the seam ratchet + OpenAPI contract tests, builds on node-2 (never in the live tree), deploys through health-checked promote scripts with auto-rollback: nxeon (existing promote-production.sh), cyrus app + api + worker (`promote-cyrus.sh`), landing (rsync to /var/www/cyrus.my or Cloudflare Pages), admin. Shared packages guarantee "same behaviour" across nxeon.cloud, cyrus.my and the Nxeon tab; API contracts are versioned (v1 stays until v2 proven; expand/contract DB migrations; N and N-1 compatible) so deploy order never breaks anything; flags allow dark launches and instant rollback. Rule kept: never edit or build in /opt/nxeon; worktrees + devhost; deploy only through the promote scripts.

## 8. Gaps and improvements to remember
Teams/shared projects; public developer API + personal API keys with docs.cyrus.my; mod marketplace/NxLabs listings, ratings, reports, and the parked Mojang EULA/marketplace question; moderation SLAs; DMCA/takedown process and counter-notice; per-user AI spend caps; data residency/GDPR export-delete; accessibility audit; email deliverability for cyrus.my; Discord/community; localisation (later); webhooks retry dashboards; load test before launch; disaster-recovery drill; customer support macros; pricing page truthfulness (no invented prices or stats); .my domain registrant/legal pages.

## 9. Today (suggested order)
1. You: confirm section 1 decisions (10 min). 2. Me: finish landing review -> publish to cyrus.my. 3. Agents (bundled, frugal): r36 bridge (running), then P3 scaffold + P4 Platform API (two Opus bundles), P2 once you give a Nxeon-zone token. 4. You: real-client test day and eval budget whenever convenient (they gate launch, not the refactor).

Research claims are labelled VERIFIED or UNVERIFIED in those files; this plan inherits their labels and adds none of its own. Sizes are S/M/L effort.
4	
5	## 1. What we are building
6	A real game-mod **engine**, not a prompt box. The source of truth is a typed, versioned **mod project**; the AI is the author and editor inside it; deterministic generators, validators and a real-server test harness turn the project into artifacts; studios and designers edit the same project; mods compose into Mod Packs; users can bring their own mods. Minecraft is adapter #1 on a game-agnostic core.
7	
8	**Principles**
9	1. Engine first: every feature must be typed, validated, testable, editable and composable. A prompt wrapper is not a feature.
10	2. Evidence over claims: no status ("built", "tested", "supported") that did not actually run. Compile, scan, boot test and functional test are separate checks.
11	3. Foundation for other games: shared core behind interfaces; per-game adapters (Section 4.10).
12	4. Honest about limits: the router tells users what a vanilla client can and cannot do.
13	5. Dependencies decide order, not enthusiasm (the review found five dependency inversions in the first schedule; this plan fixes them).
14	
15	## 2. Decisions already made by the owner
16	- Plan tiers: Free and Katara get no studios; **Saka gets Sound Studio + Sound Library; the top plan (`all`, includes Yakko) gets everything** including Texture Studio + Texture Library. Tiers are cumulative.
17	- **Automatic asset generation follows the user's plan and access** (same gate whether Cyrus, the studio or a library creates the asset).
18	- **Mod Packs are not gated by plan. Importing your own mod to work on it is not gated by plan.**
19	- Asset libraries and studios are top priorities; the owner's 514-file sound library is the Sound Library seed.
20	- Everything in scope, ambitious timeline; launch is months away. Research ran as limited Sonnet agents; no parallel agent sprawl.
21	- Parked by the owner ("later"): Mojang EULA / marketplace question, other-platform AI policies (Modrinth etc.), licence review of dependencies. Not worked in this plan.
22	
23	**Defaults I set (change any of them):**
24	- Gate semantics: gates apply to **creating or editing** assets. Installing, keeping, rebuilding unchanged and exporting existing project assets is never gated. The router downgrades (no custom asset) instead of erroring, and gating fails closed when token state is unknown.
25	- Banshee on 1.21.x = custom skin + full sound set on a vanilla-model mob; **animated custom-model creatures are 26.x first** (BetterModel v3 needs Java 25).
26	- Generated mods stay on `plugin.yml` (Paper's `paper-plugin.yml` is still experimental).
27	- Gameplay Designers, full creature pipeline and worldgen come after the foundation, assets and composition (they are mini-languages each).
28	
29	## 2b. Built to stand alone later (owner decision, 2026-10-10)
30	Cyrus stays a part of Nxeon for at least the next few months (to build a solid foundation and gather months of real Nxeon-customer usage data), then may become its own product. So:
31	- **Nothing breaks and nothing changes for customers:** same sign-in, same accounts, same wallet, same billing. No separate Cyrus login now.
32	- **Design for the split from day one (cheap now, expensive later):** Cyrus code reaches Nxeon only through a small **host seam** (sign-in/user, plan and billing, server access for install, storage, notifications). New code must not add new direct imports of Nxeon internals; where one is unavoidable it goes behind a named adapter. Cyrus tables stay Cyrus-prefixed with opaque ids for users/servers (no new foreign keys into Nxeon tables). The build service already stands alone; the engine core, asset pipelines, Test Flight and pack hosting already live under `lib/cyrus/` and stay game- and host-agnostic.
33	- **Later, when separating:** Nxeon implements the host side as an API (list servers, push plugin/pack/config, restart); a standalone Cyrus gets its own sign-in, wallet and billing, own database, and a standalone export (jar and pack download). The Kodely-to-Nxeon partner API is the existing pattern.
34	- **Not now:** no code that exists only to prepare the split beyond the seam rule and a coupling map.
35	
36	## 3. Reality check on the facts (from the research)
37	- Cyrus builds only 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/1.21.11 on JDK 21. Compile is plain `javac --release 21 -proc:none` against a Paper-only classpath (Gradle only builds classpath files). 4 of 6 explicitly versioned Paper servers on Nxeon already run 26.x, so version support is a top lever. 26.x needs Java 25. **Correction (checked on Paper's Fill API and Maven, 2026-10-10):** stable builds exist only for 26.1.2 (build 74) and 26.2 (build 133); 26.3 has only alpha/beta builds, so the version research was wrong that 26.3 is stable. The 26.x lane starts with **26.2**, then 26.1.2; 26.3 stays preview and unpinned until Paper ships a stable build. The registry now holds the exact pins and server-jar hashes.
38	- No ModSpec, project/revision store, asset manifest or import flow exist. A "project" is a chain of `ModBuild` rows. `textures/` does item textures only; `sfx.ts` is interface sounds only. The Mods installer treats resource packs as unsupported. `packFormatFor` is wrong for 26.x (returns 75; 26.1 is 76-84). Plan tiers gate models only; the single gate is `gateBuild` at `create.ts:72`, bypassed when tokens are off.
39	- `server.properties` holds one resource pack; Paper's `Player#addResourcePack(UUID, ...)` allows several and `setResourcePack` is deprecated.
40	- A vanilla client with a server-pushed pack plus datapack can show items, weapons, armor, food, display-entity mobs, glyph HUDs, GUIs, enchantments, recipes, advancements, bosses, abilities, commands, sounds, biomes and structures. Client-mod-only: brand-new block types, native entity models, free-form HUD widgets, custom keybinds, custom sky.
41	- Build service auth: it can run on a subscription login. Before ANY public launch, switch to an API key and re-measure cost (not blocking development now).
42	- Jars are not reproducible today (`jar --create` without `--date`).
43	
44	## 4. Engine design
45	### 4.1 Mod project model + revisions (size L)
46	Typed project: `ModSpec`/content IR (items, mobs, abilities, GUIs, quests, recipes, loot, biomes...), code files, assets, datapacks, config, dependencies, tests, requirement IDs. Stored as immutable revisions with diffs; each revision traces to exact inputs and toolchain; the last passing revision is always preserved. `schemaVersion` with explicit migrations; JSON Schema as the portable contract, Zod types in code. New tables (project, revision, asset, namespace) need an owner-approved DB migration deploy. Chat history is not the project.
47	
48	### 4.2 Registries and reserved namespaces (S-M)
49	Capability registry, **version registry**, **identifier registry**, asset registry with provenance. Each project reserves a namespace `nx_<hash>` at creation so IDs, keys, permissions, sound keys, glyph ranges and model paths are collision-free by construction. Version registry holds exact pack format per version (one `pack.mcmeta` style per version family), JDK, classpath hash, capability flags (item model definitions from 1.21.4; Dialog API 1.21.7+; Folia support), status (`preview/supported/deprecated/blocked`). Contract-tested against Paper's Fill API.
50	
51	### 4.3 Capability router + task spec (M)
52	After the prompt check: classify what the request needs (plugin / plugin + resource pack / datapack / future client mod), disclose limits, show an editable plan and acceptance criteria before tokens are spent. One schema: this is the Master Plan's `CyrusTaskSpec`, the Roadmap's Mod Specification and the asset manifest. Tier gate is applied here and again inside the build service request.
53	
54	### 4.4 Generators, build and reproducibility (M)
55	Deterministic generators emit code/data/packs for common mechanics from the IR; free-form AI code is the fallback. Build: `javac` per version lane (JDK 21 and JDK 25 side by side, per-version `--release`, classpath files fetched by checksum, exact stable pin), scan, package. Make jars byte-stable (`jar --date`, sorted inputs); record **engine release id** (prompt version + sheets + rules + scanner hash + image digest), source/classpath/output hashes, scan report and SBOM per artifact. Rename CYR-004 to "immutable javac/classpath/template".
56	
57	### 4.5 Managed plugins, Pack Loader, pack hosting (M)
58	- **ManagedPlugin** records: pinned version per Minecraft family, installed on first dependent mod, ref-counted, not user-removable while depended on. Hosts the Pack Loader and BetterModel.
59	- **Nxeon Pack Loader**: sends N packs by UUID with `addResourcePack`, per-pack required/optional, accept-rate telemetry, Geyser/Floodgate detection. `server.properties` only as fallback. Conflict engine detects an existing pack owner (ResourcePackManager, Oraxen, Nexo).
60	- **Pack hosting**: object storage on an Nxeon domain (provider not named to customers), content-addressed immutable URLs `/p/<sha1>.zip`, size caps, retention GC; keep it off the primary node.
61	
62	### 4.6 Test Flight (M, lite first)
63	Disposable Paper server per target version on node-2 (MEASURED 2026-10-10 with Test Flight lite: 26.x 10.4-10.8 s boot, 722-803 MB peak RSS; 1.21.11 on JDK 21 18.0 s, 878 MB; whole flight 12-20 s; see docs "Cyrus Test Flight (R0)"): boot, plugin enabled, RCON commands, `datapack list`, log matcher, clean shutdown. Later: MockBukkit logic tests, Mineflayer scenario bots (MIT, supports through 26.1), performance scenarios. Honest per-check status table; no "success" if a required stage was skipped. Concurrency capped (a past node crash came from parallel builds).
64	
65	### 4.7 Asset pipeline and studios
66	Shared studio core + per-game profile. Minecraft = pixel profile.
67	- **Texture** (top plan): LLM writes a pixel spec (palette + shapes), deterministic renderer draws it (raise the 400-op / 16-64 px limits for skins and larger atlases), optional pixel-model candidates later; per-mod **Style DNA** (palette ramps, outline rule, noise) for consistency; per-version validation; AI edits arrive as non-destructive candidates.
68	- **Sound** (Saka+): `SoundSpec` (events -> layers -> processing); tag the 514-file library by filename category; synthesis presets; processing in the browser from WAV, **server-side ffmpeg/libvorbis to mono Ogg Vorbis**; new namespaced sound keys played by the plugin (and silence the vanilla base mob; never override vanilla keys globally); mandatory subtitle keys. A complete mob set: ambient, hurt, death, step, attack, ability, spawn.
69	- **Models** (26.x first): `RigSpec` compiled by Nxeon code (3 archetypes, 5 procedural clips) to .bbmodel for **BetterModel** (MIT, pinned managed plugin). Handgun and similar items use static item models with display transforms, sounds and particles, no engine. Do not embed Blockbench (GPL app); do not depend on ModelEngine/FreeMinecraftModels/CraftEngine.
70	- **Quality bar**: rubric + metrics (texture palette size, contrast, edge density, banding, transparent policy; sound mono, true peak, loudness band per role, silence ratio) plus a vision-model judge calibrated on 100 owner-labelled samples; owner reviews a gallery.
71	- **Studios**: v1 minimal (miniPaint MIT stopgap or a small pixel editor; wavesurfer.js BSD waveform with trim/fade/layer and JSON edit recipes), then the full editors in R3. Library browsing follows the studio gate.
72	
73	### 4.8 Conflict engine and Mod Packs (L)
74	- **Server inventory** first: read-only scan of jars' descriptors, `server.properties`, datapacks, existing pack owners. This is the conflict engine's input (and the "Server Doctor" feature below).
75	- **Static classes**: plugin names, commands/aliases (incl. Brigadier root literals and vanilla overrides), permissions, depend/softdepend/loadbefore DAG, api-version/Java/Folia, registered events + priorities, NamespacedKey/PDC keys, legacy `custom_model_data` integers and `item_model` keys, recipe keys, sound event keys, single-owner resources (Vault economy/permission provider, chat renderer, tab list, sidebar, world rules), datapack `replace:true` tags and double-overridden vanilla ids, resource-pack whole-file overrides, `sounds.json`/atlas/lang merges, font codepoint overlap, unmergeable shaders, budget classes (display entities, tasks, pack size).
76	- **Resolution**: reserved namespaces prevent most clashes; command alias rewrites; priority ordering; Pack Loader stacking; evaluate Weld/Beet (MIT) as an offline merge subprocess behind golden tests. Severity report: blocking / warn / info.
77	- **Dynamic**: one combined boot and one differential boot per changed mod; pairwise only for statically flagged pairs.
78	- **Mod Pack**: an Nxeon manifest shaped like mrpack (files with path/sha1/sha512/downloads/env, override dirs, platform=paper). Third-party jars by URL + hash, only Cyrus-built artifacts embedded. Versioned, changelog, compatibility matrix, combined test report; installs and rolls back as one unit; never contains Paper/vanilla jars. Not gated by plan.
79	
80	### 4.9 Import your own mod (L)
81	Source-only first: copy `src/main/java|resources`, drop and ignore the uploader's build files (their build is never run), compile with the service template and a **curated checksum-pinned dependency allowlist** (also the basis for first-class integrations: Vault, LuckPerms, PlaceholderAPI as soft bridge). Unsupported: Kotlin, Lombok, annotation processors. Ingestion limits (zip-slip, zip bomb ratio, nested jars, multi-release, class major), no execution at ingestion, ownership attestation record, detected licence, public sharing only with consent. Two scan profiles: strict for generated, **attested/imported** with warnings and no "safe" claim. Imported source becomes revision 0 and uses the same change planner, tests, versions and install path. Jar-only imports are analysis and diagnosis only (decompile for navigation, never into shared knowledge). Not gated by plan; model use and assets follow tokens and the asset gates.
82	
83	### 4.10 Per-game adapter contract (S, define in R0)
84	Artifact types and routes; toolchain profile and deny-list scan; version registry; knowledge pack; asset formats and **delivery** (Minecraft: server-pushed pack; Valheim: client zip; Terraria/Palworld: none; tModLoader: client mod); install rules; test lane; maturity level. Add `game` to every id and registry. Texture/Sound studios light up only where the adapter declares an asset format and delivery path. A realistic 3D/PBR profile is a later track; build only the interfaces now.
85	
86	### 4.11 Data packs (M)
87	Typed spec -> per-version emitters (the AI never hand-writes JSON); schema source vanilla-mcdoc (MIT); static validation then boot a real headless Paper and test over RCON. MVP: recipes, loot, advancements, tags, functions, enchantments. Worldgen (biomes, structures, dimensions) later; `/reload` does not reload worldgen, so those changes need a restart.
88	
89	## 5. Roadmap (ordered by dependency)
90	Calendar note: the review estimated R0-R2 at about 5-7 weeks including owner waits (UNVERIFIED judgement). The owner has beaten estimates; treat these as sequencing and relative size, not promises. (T) = real Minecraft client needed, (O) = owner action.
91	
92	### R0 Foundation (about 4 working days)
93	| Day | Deliver | Done when |
94	|---|---|---|
95	| 1 | Launch gates (verify hardened scan live (O), per-build engine-release record, paired flag guard, free-build abuse limit, per-build cost cap). Version registry with exact pack formats; fix `packFormatFor`; reproducible jars; JDK 25 beside 21 on node-2; classpath files by checksum; pin exact stable 26.x; nightly Fill check creates a "preview" row | Can prove what built every mod; 26.x compiles on node-2; pack numbers verified |
96	| 2 | Project model + revision store (DB migration (O)), ModSpec/IR, identifier registry + reserved namespaces, GameAdapter interface, minimal capability router, server-side tier gate (fail closed) | Spec stored per project; router explains limits; gate matrix test (4 plans x create/edit/keep/install) passes |
97	| 3 | ManagedPlugin mechanism, pack hosting (object storage + domain (O)), Pack Loader, **Test Flight lite** | A pack reaches a test server through the Pack Loader; boot gate runs on every build |
98	| 4 | Server inventory (read-only); eval harness extended (100+ prompts, per-version matrix, asset prompts) | Inventory report on a real server; baseline pass rate recorded per version |
99	
100	### R1 Assets (about 5 days)
101	| Day | Deliver | Done when |
102	|---|---|---|
103	| 5 | Texture slice: spec -> renderer -> validated pack; Style DNA; library of vanilla-style presets + uploads; hybrid JAR + pack install/uninstall (T) | Custom item shows its texture in a real client |
104	| 6 | Sound slice: tag library, synth presets, server-side mono Ogg, `sounds.json`, subtitles, multi-event per item/mob (T) | Right sounds play per event in a real client; Katara/free correctly blocked |
105	| 7 | Static 3D item models (the Glock) with display transforms, sounds, particles; vanilla-mob reskin + full sound set (banshee on 1.21.x) (T) | Glock and a banshee skin + sounds install and play |
106	| 8 | Studios v1: open a mod's assets, edit, re-push pack, revisions, library browsing, quality rubric + gallery (T) | Customer edits a texture/sound and sees it on the server; owner approves the gallery |
107	| 9 | Hardening: access test matrix, cost estimates per asset op, asset cost caps (2 critique rounds), caching by spec hash | Asset ops priced by measured work; no free bypass |
108	
109	### R1b Full Texture and Sound Studios (owner priority, added 2026-10-10; Opus for the editor cores)
110	Moved forward from R3: the studios are a top priority, so the full editors come right after the first asset slice and before composition.
111	- **Texture Studio (top plan):** full pixel editor (layers, undo/redo, palettes and ramps, selection, tiling and 3D item preview, onion-skin for animated textures), library browsing and search, Style DNA applied across a whole mod, AI edits as non-destructive candidates with before/after diffs, reference-image-to-spec through a vision model, asset history, the quality rubric as a real review screen.
112	- **Sound Studio (Saka and up):** full waveform editor (zoom, regions, trim, fade, gain, pitch/time, layering, spectrum, loudness and true-peak readouts), library browsing and search by tag, synthesis presets, per-event mob/item sound sets, subtitle keys, non-destructive edit recipes, server-side Ogg export, asset history with waveform diffs.
113	- **Both:** shared studio core with per-game profiles (Minecraft pixel profile first); plan-tier gates enforced server-side; library follows the studio gate.
114	- **Done when:** a customer builds a complete set (e.g. banshee skin plus attack/hurt/death sounds) entirely in the studios without touching a prompt, and a real client shows and plays it (T).
115	- R3 keeps only animated creatures, gameplay designers and playtest scripts.
116	
117	### Item model states and display contexts (owner question, 2026-10-10; queued after Studio UI part 1)
118	Today the pack builder emits ONE flat model per texture (handheld parent): one look, no states. Owner needs: how an item looks dropped, in an inventory slot, in first-person and third-person hand, on the head, in an item frame; and stateful items (a bow idle vs pulled back; a gun aiming/reloading).
119	- **ItemModelSpec v1** (new, in the asset spec): per-context display transforms (gui, ground, fixed/item frame, first/third person right+left hand, head) with per-category defaults (sword, tool, bow, gun, wand, shield) the owner/studio can override; named STATES each with a model/texture and the condition that selects it.
120	- **Mechanism (1.21.4+ item model definitions; names UNVERIFIED, must be checked against the docs and real servers before building):** `condition` on using_item, `range_dispatch` on use_duration/pull for pull stages, `select` on display_context, and plugin-set custom_model_data flags/strings (e.g. reloading, aiming); a custom bow is built on real bow behaviour with our item_model; a custom gun uses a consumable-style 'using' state for aiming and plugin flags for reload/cooldown. Limits: no free-form animation (texture frame animation via .mcmeta and fast model switching only; no real recoil). 1.21.1 needs the legacy predicate/custom-model-data overrides path (later).
121	- **Generator:** emits items/<name>.json (definition with conditions/range/select), one model JSON per state with its display block, and tests with golden hashes; the build prompt tells the plugin which states exist and the flag keys; registry capability checked per version.
122	- **Studio:** context switcher (hotbar, dropped, first-person, third-person, item frame, head) and a STATE scrubber (idle, pull 1-3, aim, reload) in the preview; correct 'in hand' placement (the grip in the hand: the first fix already requested of the Studio UI agent).
123	- **Later:** true 3D cuboid item models (the model pipeline) for guns/bows that should not be extruded sprites.
124	
125	### Asset Library (owner requirement, 2026-10-10): one proper, cataloged, searchable library for sounds AND textures
126	The owner wants every asset cataloged and organized, not just filename-tagged. Shared design for both libraries:
127	- **Taxonomy as data** (committed JSON, not code): primary category, multi-valued **use cases** (where a mod uses it), free tags, descriptors derived from measured data (sound: duration class, intensity, pitch band, loopable heuristic, channels; texture: size, palette ramp, transparency, tileable, style), synonym table, and a licence/provenance ledger per asset (never asserting originality that has not been documented).
128	- **Sound categories:** Weapons (gunshot, reload, cocking, ricochet, melee swing, clash, bow), Creatures & Voices, Impacts & Destruction, Movement, Environment & Ambience, Doors & Mechanisms, UI & Alerts, Crowd & Reactions. **Use cases:** weapon_fire, weapon_reload, weapon_impact, melee, mob_ambient/hurt/death/attack/step, ability_cast, magic, boss_event, ui_notification, pickup_reward, block_interaction, door_mechanism, ambience_world, weather, explosion (gunshot + reload are both also tagged `weapon`).
129	- **Texture categories:** Items (weapon, tool, armor, food, potion, misc), Blocks (stone, wood, ore, plant, glass, decorative), Entity skins (humanoid, quadruped, flyer, ghost), GUI (button, panel, icon, HUD piece), Particles, and **Style DNA presets** (palette ramps, outline rule, noise level); sources: Cyrus-authored original template specs, the customer's uploads, textures from the customer's own projects, later community-shared; every texture carries provenance + licence status and passes the quality bar.
130	- **Search (both):** free text with synonym expansion and ranking (exact tag > category > name words), facets/filters, pagination, "similar to"; Postgres full-text first, embeddings only later; library browsing follows the studio plan gate (sound = Saka and up, texture = top plan).
131	- **Builds now (R1, by the sound agent):** the sound library manifest + taxonomy + search API + a human catalog report for the owner to review. **Next:** the texture library (starter template specs authored as DSL, quality-checked) and a **unified catalog layer** (`lib/cyrus/library`) that serves sounds, textures and later models through one interface, with customer uploads stored as Cyrus-prefixed records; then the browse/search UI inside the studios (design mockups in progress).
132	
133	
134	
135	
136	### Motion, Animation and Effects: FOUNDATION (owner decision, 2026-10-10)
137	Owner: motion/animation/effects is foundational and NOT Minecraft-only: AI (or a human) creates the motion a mod needs (banshee walk cycle, gun cock/fire/reload, car driving with doors opening and a character getting in, explosions, fire, water), with LIVE playable simulation in the studio, tied to the Texture and Sound studios; per-game specifics are handled in adapters when each game is added, but the foundation exists now.
138	State today: pieces only. Have: `spawn_particles` in the designer (budgeted), creature clips (BetterModel), item model states (bow pull, gun aim/reload), Model Studio layer 2 pose/animation timeline (in build; told to keep it game-neutral and extensible), sound library, catalog. Missing: the game-neutral Motion core.
139	- **Motion core (proposal):** tracks with typed kinds (transform, particle, sound-cue, light/material, event/state-machine), clips, triggers from the ability graph (`play_effect`), deterministic sampler, playback clock API (viewport exposes it), simulator contract, per-game exporter/adapter contract, presets in the catalog as kind `effect`/`motion`, caps (entities, particles, duration).
140	- **First slice that proves it end to end:** gun fire/reload state machine + a door hinge in Minecraft display entities, with sound cues from the library and a muzzle-flash particle preset.
141	- **Steps:** (1) Sonnet research R-motion-effects.md (running), (2) Opus architecture + design + mockups, (3) build core + Minecraft exporter + studio timeline/preview, (4) vehicle rig + character attach: NOT a Minecraft target (owner clarified 2026-10-10); the neutral core must be able to express it, the build waits for the first vehicle-capable game (FiveM/RedM etc.), (5) other games per adapter.
142	
143	### Config and Stats Studio: FOUNDATION (owner request, 2026-10-10)
144	Owner: manual configuration/stat editors for every kind of mod (mob speed/health/attack damage and speed, weapon fire rate/reload/ammo, ability cooldowns, shop prices, boss phases...), so nobody must prompt the AI to change a number; Cyrus must know which tunables to OFFER per mod category; stats with a visual (walk speed, attack speed, scale) reflect live in the viewport/motion simulation. Game-neutral schema, per-game exporters.
145	State today: only the designers have it (every number becomes a config.yml setting; `edit without regenerating`; /<plugin> params|reload; `planDesignEdit` exposed but NOT wired); plain AI plugins are only told to 'put tunable values in config.yml'; imported mods have their own config.yml; no studio form editor; no category-aware tunable templates.
146	Plan: ConfigSpec (typed params, units, safe ranges, applies live/reload/restart, visual links), category templates (mob, melee, gun, armor, ability, boss, shop, quest, minigame, world, item, utility), the AI declares tunables and the build verifies they are read, values-only revisions delivered through the delivery orchestrator (no model, no build), schema inference for imported mods, presets, Config page in the studio shell. Agent launched (Opus, branch feature/cyrus-r23-config). Owner decision: ungated (editing numbers is not asset creation), recommended.
147	
148	### R2 Composition, data packs, import (about 7 days)
149	| Day | Deliver | Done when |
150	|---|---|---|
151	| 10-11 | Static conflict engine on the inventory; severity report; reserved-namespace behaviour; mutation corpus (take a good mod, collide IDs) | Seeded conflicts caught with the right class and severity |
152	| 12 | Mod Pack Builder: manifest, merge (Weld/Beet evaluation), combined boot + differential boots, install/rollback as one unit | Two conflicting mods are caught, resolved or blocked; pack installs and rolls back as a unit |
153	| 13-14 | Datapack MVP: typed emitters per version, mcdoc validation, boot + RCON check | Valid datapack loads on every listed version |
154	| 15-16 | Import (source-only): ingestion limits, allowlist, attestation, strict vs attested scan, revision 0, change planner | An uploaded simple plugin source is edited by prompt, rebuilt, scanned, tested, installed; history kept |
155	| 16 | Public pass-rate page + evidence badges (boot-tested on exact version, scan hash, SBOM) | Numbers come from real runs |
156	
157	### R3 Creatures, full studios, designers (L; after R2 is stable)
158	- **26.x creature pipeline**: BetterModel managed plugin; RigSpec compiler; 3 archetypes; 5 clips; banshee end to end; hitboxes and attacks; performance budget per server (T).
159	- **Full Texture and Sound Studios**: layers/undo/palettes/selection/tiling preview/onion skin; waveform, spectrum, layering; reference-image-to-spec via a vision model; asset history with diffs.
160	- **Gameplay Designers**, one at a time: Custom Item Designer; ability/event graph (typed triggers -> conditions -> actions compiled to validated code, no arbitrary scripts) with a verified component library; then GUI, quests/NPCs, bosses, progression, minigames. Auto-generated Dialog config screens (1.21.7+).
161	- **Playtest scripts** from spec acceptance criteria (Mineflayer).
162	
163	### R4 World and reach (L)
164	Biomes, structures, dimensions (restart rule); glyph HUDs with honest limits (avoid core shaders); "Try it" throwaway server link; multi-version build from one ModSpec; legacy `custom_model_data` emitter for 1.21.1; Server Doctor for servers with no Cyrus mods; mod health telemetry (opt-in).
165	
166	### R5 Beyond Minecraft Java (own programmes)
167	Fabric client-mod pipeline (narrow); the other five games as adapters (multi-game prompt, per-game maturity ladder); realistic 3D/PBR asset profile; Bedrock conversion. Each starts only when the previous layers are stable.
168	
169	## 6. Cross-cutting
170	- **Testing/eval**: extend the existing harness (28 prompts, 28/28 built, 13/13 loaded on v6) to 100+ prompts per version; golden pack snapshots (canonical JSON + sorted file list + sha1); property tests for merge laws (idempotent, order-stable, no key loss); javap-verified API sheets in CI; contract test of the version registry; mutation corpus for conflicts. Per-version pass rates published only when measured.
171	- **Quality bar**: Style DNA, rubric metrics, vision-judge calibration, owner gallery sign-off.
172	- **Pricing**: show an estimate before building; price assets by measured work; no charge if validation fails before delivery; per-feature reserve rows (reconcile `katara/saka/yakko` vs `katara/saka/all` naming); free tier gets no assets and per-device/IP caps.
173	- **Operations**: treat prompt + sheets + rules + scanner + image as one engine release with canary and auto-rollback on eval regression; per-feature kill switches (asset generation, import, packs); node-2 capacity budget for test servers; prompt-injection hygiene (imported text only as quoted data, no network for the model, path allow-list on diffs).
174	- **Security**: scanner remains a policy check, not proof; fail closed; import profiles warn honestly; supply-chain pinning (sha256, image digests, lockfiles).
175	- **Telemetry funnel**: prompt -> spec -> build -> pass -> install -> pack accepted -> player joined -> day-7 retention; gate impressions and upgrade conversion.
176	
177	## 7. Risks
178	| Risk | Mitigation |
179	|---|---|
180	| Schedule: sizes in the research sum to roughly 25-35 engineer-weeks for the asset/composition/designer scope | Dependency-ordered phases; real-client and owner waits scheduled; creature/designers/worldgen after the foundation |
181	| Real-client tests (T) cannot be automated | Name a standing tester; small matrix per asset day |
182	| BetterModel v3/v2 split and Java 25 | Creatures 26.x first; pinned managed plugin; test before relying on 1.21.1 |
183	| Paper experimental APIs (paper-plugin.yml, data components) | Generated mods on plugin.yml; isolate experiments in the Nxeon-owned loader; monthly CI |
184	| Beta builds via floating coordinates | Pin exact stable; nightly check |
185	| Import hardness (dependencies, scanner bans reflection/network that legitimate plugins use) | Allowlist + attested profile; source-only first |
186	| Scanner false sense of safety | Honest labels; no "safe" claim for imports |
187	| Cost blowout from asset critique loops | Cap rounds, cache by spec hash, per-build cost cap |
188	| Public pass-rate claims | Publish only measured numbers per version |
189	| Build service auth (subscription login) | API key + re-measured pricing before ANY public launch |
190	
191	## 8. Owner actions to line up
192	VM 88001 update and image rebuild (JDK 25 beside 21) and the hardened scan check; DB migration deploy approval (project/revision tables); object storage + domain for packs; a standing person with Minecraft for (T) days (and later Fabric); confirm or change the defaults in Section 2; weekly-usage allowance for the build weeks; API-key switch before public launch.
193	
194	## 9. Open questions
195	1. Is the banshee-on-1.21.x default (skin + sounds) acceptable, with animated creatures on 26.x first?
196	2. Confirm the gate semantics default (create/edit gated; install/keep/export never).
197	3. Who is the standing tester and on which days?
198	4. Do you want Server Doctor (scan any customer server for conflicts) as an early acquisition feature?
199	5. Which object storage and domain for packs?
200	
201	## 10. Where the details live
202	`E-versions.md` (version facts, registry), `G-gaps.md` (code audit with file:line), `A-content.md` and `A2-datapacks.md` (content feasibility, datapacks), `B-models.md` (creatures, RigSpec), `C-texture.md` and `D-sound.md` (studios), `F-quality-market.md` (competitors, test tooling), `GAPS-AND-IDEAS.md` (red-team findings, resources, ranked features), `RESEARCH-PLAN.md` (history, four-document reconciliation).
203

# Cyrus build: what exists and what needs the owner (updated 2026-10-10)

Nothing below is deployed, merged to main, migrated in production, or switched on. All work is on branches, verified on node-2 / devhost.

## Branches and worktrees (chain; later branches contain earlier ones)
- `feature/cyrus-r0` (/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r0): version registry, launch-pair guard, starter-grant guard, reproducible jars, engine core (spec, revisions, namespaces, router, asset gate), Test Flight, pack delivery (pack host, managed plugins, Pack Loader), 26.x lane (inert), eval set (124 prompts).
- `feature/cyrus-r1` (/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r1): texture slice, sound slice (+ library manifest/taxonomy/search), texture library + unified catalog layer.
- `feature/cyrus-r2` (/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r2): r1 merged in + server inventory, conflict engine, Mod Packs. **The current integration branch.**
- `feature/cyrus-r3` (cyrus-r3): import-your-own-mod. DONE and merged into r2.
- `feature/cyrus-r4` (cyrus-r4): Data Pack Studio backend. DONE and merged into r2 (server.js/prompts.js conflicts resolved).
- `feature/cyrus-r5` (cyrus-r5): Studio UI part 1: shell, Texture Studio, locked states, library browser (in progress, from r2).
- `feature/cyrus-r6` (cyrus-r6): animated creature pipeline, BetterModel 3.5.0, 26.x first. DONE and merged into r2 (34 conflict blocks resolved; 1211 Cyrus/builder tests pass, tsc clean).
- `feature/cyrus-r7` (cyrus-r7): gameplay designer engine (items + ability graph + 17-component library). DONE and merged into r2 (31 conflict blocks; 1325 Cyrus/builder tests pass; tsc clean).
- `feature/cyrus-r8` (cyrus-r8): worldgen datapacks (custom dimensions/biomes/structures). DONE and merged into r2 (1394 Cyrus/builder tests pass, tsc clean).
- `feature/cyrus-r9` (cyrus-r9): Sound Studio UI. DONE and merged into r2 (1468 Cyrus/builder tests pass, tsc clean).
- `feature/cyrus-r10` (cyrus-r10): item model states + display contexts (bow pull, gun aim/reload, 8 contexts, studio In-game preview). DONE and merged into r2 (1429 Cyrus/builder tests pass, tsc clean).
- `feature/cyrus-r11` (cyrus-r11): GUI menu + quest designers, extends the design kind. DONE and merged into r2 (1531 Cyrus/builder tests pass, tsc clean).
- `feature/cyrus-r12`: integration/delivery (release record, Test Flight gate, delivery orchestrator with proven rollback, sound relay, admin read model). DONE, merged into r2 together with r13-foundation (1596 tests pass).
- Studio UI part 1 (r5: shell, Texture Studio, library browser, locked states) is DONE and merged into r2.
- Queued next: Sound Studio UI, item model states and display contexts, animated creature pipeline (26.x), gameplay designers, then R4/R5 of the master plan.

## Switches (all OFF; fail closed)
`cyrus_studio_public_enabled` + `cyrus_tok_live` (must move together; guard built), `cyrus_import_enabled`, `cyrus_studios_enabled`, `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO`, `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL`, `CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL=1` (real plugin/pack install), `CYRUS_MODPACK_INSTALL_REAL=1`, `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1` (until set, customer builds get synth sounds only), `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh` (render host), pack storage env (`CYRUS_PACK_PUBLIC_BASE` + S3 settings).

## Needs your approval or action
1. **Production migrations** (additive, new tables only): `prisma/manual-migrations/2026-10-10-cyrus-engine-core.sql` (4 tables + a trigger that must be run by hand), `2026-10-10-cyrus-managed-plugins.sql` (2 tables) then `scripts/cyrus-seed-managed-plugins.ts`. More may be added by in-progress agents (they report).
2. **VM 88001** (the deploy script /root/agent-notes/deploy-modbuilder.sh now copies every needed file incl. registry.json and deps.json; the Dockerfile COPY list was missing textures/sound modules before and is fixed and test-guarded): rebuild the build-service image with the new files (jar.js, textures.js, sound files, texture-example.json, datapack/import files when done), the JDK 25 build args, and make `registry.json` available inside the container; verify the hardened scan is live; check `/health` `auth` (API key vs subscription) and switch to an API key **before any public launch**; then one real build to confirm reproducible jars and the asset sections.
3. **Pack hosting**: choose storage provider/bucket (any S3 API; R2 has free egress), the public pack domain (`CYRUS_PACK_PUBLIC_BASE`), retention for unused packs; deploy the Pack Loader jar to the worker host.
4. **Sound library**: confirm Excelerator.tech is yours, document the source per file group, then set `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1`; write the customer-facing sound licence; review `sound-library-catalog.md`; set the render path (ssh key to node-2, worker only).
5. **Reviews**: texture contact sheets (`texture-library-sheets/`), the studio design mockups (`/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/`), the 7 design defaults I chose (plan names Katara/Saka/Yakko, token cost shown on asset edits, packs optional with per-mod required option, 'Mob skin: coming soon', read-only mobile approve, full-page editors).
6. **Decisions**: should a Mod Pack with open warnings install without the user acknowledging them? (r29 Mod Pack API now REQUIRES acknowledgement of every open warning, per the recommendation; tell me if you want it relaxed.) Import attestation wording and rate limits (when the import agent reports).
7. **Real-client test day** (someone with Minecraft): pack download and accept prompt, textures, item previews, sounds and subtitles, Bedrock note. Nothing resource-pack related is verified in a real client yet.
8. **Paid eval run**: approve a number of real builds and budget (the eval set is 124 prompts; a full multi-version run is 226 builds; ~30 texture prompts first); a baseline file is saved after the first run.
9. Delete when finished: `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/r0-26x` (~2 GB) and old tmp dirs.

## Known limits (honest)
No real model build has been run for texture/sound/datapack/import sections, so the AI's output quality is unverified. No real client has loaded a pack. The vanilla-lookalike texture check is a stub. Test Flight runs one flight at a time with no container limits. 26.3 has no stable Paper build (only alpha/beta).

content.thinking:
I'm noticing some default value hints are misleading, likely because the pattern matching is picking up comment-style assignments like "CYRUS_API_V1=1" as if they were true defaults. I should restrict that matching pattern to only apply within actual shell files, catching things like `${X:-}` syntax or line-start assignments, rather than scanning arbitrary comments.

The doc hints are also too noisy and lengthy, pulling header comments that aren't actually describing the flag. // Cyrus admin r40: Flags & kill switches. PURE (client-safe). Unit-tested in test/cyrus-admin-r40.test.ts.
//   - CYRUS_ENV_FLAGS: every CYRUS_* environment switch, grouped. These are process env on the server: the page shows
//     them READ-ONLY (on/off, or a non-secret mode value; a secret is only ever "set"/"unset") because changing one
//     needs an env edit + restart through the deploy runbook. Settings (cyrus_*) are editable: settings-catalog.ts.
//   - the launch pair: cyrus_studio_public_enabled and cyrus_tok_live always move TOGETHER (a public studio without the
//     token economy would build for free; the economy without the public studio sells nothing). Each one alone is
//     refused by validateSettingValue (editAt) and the pair action checks the typed confirmation.

## 1. Minecraft Java sound system

**sounds.json** (VERIFIED https://minecraft.wiki/w/Sounds.json)
- Lives at `assets/<namespace>/sounds.json` in a resource pack. Top level maps an **event key** (e.g. `entity.zombie.hurt`, or a custom `banshee.wail`) to `{ "replace": bool, "subtitle": "<lang key>", "sounds": [...] }`.
- Each `sounds` entry is either a bare string (file path without `.ogg`, optional `namespace:` prefix) or an object: `name`, `type` (`file` default, or `event` to reference another event), `volume` (>0, default 1), `pitch` (>0, default 1), `weight` (int, random pick bias), `strea
- Event vs file: the game plays an **event key**; the engine picks one entry from the list by weight (variants). Files are the raw Ogg Vorbis. Variants are how you avoid repetition (author 3-4 per hurt/step).
- `replace: true` discards the vanilla list for that event; false/absent appends to vanilla variants.
- Format: **Ogg Vorbis required**. **Mono = positional** (volume falls with distance); **stereo = constant volume** regardless of distance. So every mob/world sound must be mono; only music/UI may be stereo. All VERIFIED same URL.
- Custom namespaces: use `namespace:key` / `namespace:path` (VERIFIED same URL). Put a plugin's keys in its own namespace (e.g. `nxeon_banshee:`), never `minecraft:`.
- Subtitles: `subtitle` is a translation key; the text must exist in `assets/<ns>/lang/en_us.json` (UNVERIFIED detail, standard behaviour).

**What a pack can override vs add** (reasoning; UNVERIFIED in game by me)
- Override `entity.<mob>.hurt/death/ambient/step`: changes that sound for EVERY vanilla mob of that type server-wide, for each player with the pack. Fine for a total-conversion, bad for a mod that adds one "banshee" built on a zombie.
- Add new keys (`ns:banshee.wail`): triggered only by plugin code. This is the right default for Cyrus: new keys, plugin plays them, and silences the vanilla base mob (`Entity#setSilent(true)`, UNVERIFIED API name) so vanilla zombie groans do not overlap.
- Plugin playback (Paper/Bukkit): `World#playSound(Location, String key, SoundCategory, volume, pitch)` and `Player#playSound(...)` take a **string key**, so custom keys work without an enum (UNVERIFIED signatures; check against the Paper jar's javap during build sheets). Categor
- If the player lacks the pack, an unknown key plays silently, so a mod must degrade gracefully.

Method: read-only adversarial pass over everything Cyrus exposes (4 parallel readers + one real Blender probe on node-2), then fixes with tests.
Labels: **VERIFIED-TEST** = a test fails on the old code / passes on the fix; **VERIFIED-RUN** = reproduced on real software; **VERIFIED-READ** = concrete trace by reading; **UNVERIFIED** = plausible, not reproduced.

No HIGH finding: no cross-tenant read/write, no unauthenticated route, no raw proprietary sound served, no SSRF, no secrets in logs.

# Cyrus deploy runbook (owner)

Written 2026-10-10 on `feature/cyrus-r28-wiring`, against the integration branch `feature/cyrus-r2` at 702cd62d86. That commit includes the boss/encounter, HUD/glyph and motion designers.

**Updated 2026-10-10 by wiring phase 2** (`feature/cyrus-r29-wiring2`):

- the delivery enqueue path, Mod Pack routes, the playtest-in-gate path, the admin Server Doctor, the telemetry ingest and the meshgen route + job now exist, all behind switches that default OFF;
- no new migration file: telemetry still uses the existing DRAFT file, NOT applied;
- new smoke step `smoke-readonly.sh delivery`, and more checks under `flags`;
- the API contract for the UI is in `docs/CYRUS-DELIVERY-API.md`.

**Nothing in this runbook has been run.** No agent ran any of it. Agents never deploy, run production migrations, flip flags or touch VM 88001.

Do one step at a time, in order. After each step:

1. Run its smoke check.
2. Read the output.
3. Go on only when it is clean.

Every step has its own rollback.

The read-only smoke script is `scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh`, run with `[all|migrations|service|worker|flags|packs]`. Steps: `all`, `migrations`, `service`, `worker`, `flags`, `packs` and `delivery` (wiring 2: stuck delivery jobs and incomplete rollbacks). It makes no writes, no restarts and no model calls. Its DB queries run in a read-only transaction, and it never prints secret values. It exits 1 if any check FAILS.

## 0. Before you start (hazards we have already hit)

- **Never build or edit in `/opt/nxeon`.** A raw `npm run build` followed by a restart caused two outages on 2026-10-01. Code goes live only through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`, then `scripts/promote-production.sh`. Builds run on node-2 by themselves.
- **Check the primary's load first** with `uptime`. The promote cutover checks the site's health, and on an overloaded primary that check fails and the release **rolls itself back**. That rollback is safe, but your deploy did not happen. Pick a quiet hour, make sure no agent is building, and retry later if it rolled back.
- **Once you stop staging**, the promote needs `--skip-staging-check`. Without staging running, its staging-health preflight fails.
- **Never `pkill -f`.** Restart only by unit: `systemctl restart nxeon-worker` or `nxeon-web`.
- **Code review first.** Merge `feature/cyrus-r2` into `main` through a reviewed PR; it is 100+ commits. Every Cyrus feature is behind a switch that defaults to OFF, so landing the code changes nothing for customers until step 6.

## 3. Rebuild the build-service image on VM 88001

This step is independent of the site. The new image is backwards compatible: the portal sends nothing new while the switches are off.

**Script:** `scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh`. `/root/agent-notes/deploy-modbuilder.sh` is now a wrapper around it; set `REPO=` to the merged tree. Run it with `--list` first to see the file list.

**What gets copied.** Every file the Dockerfile copies, derived from the Dockerfile itself and guarded by `test/modbuilder-dockerfile.test.ts`:

- 25 service modules: `server`, `scan`, `prompts`, `route`, `precheck`, `live`, `usage`, `autofix`, `jar`, `import`, `textures`, `sound-spec`, `sounds`, `creature-spec`, `creatures`, `capabilities`, `datapack-spec`, `datapacks`, `designer-spec`, `designs`, `itemmodels`, `itemmodel-spec`, `release`, 
- Data files: `texture-example.json`, `sound-example.json`, `sound-catalog.json`, `sound-catalog.txt`, `datapack-example.json`, `worldgen-example.json`, `creature-example.json`, `designer-example.json`, `designer-gameplay-example.json`, `designer-boss-example.json`, `designer-hud-example.json`, `ite
- Directories: `template/`, `sheets/`, `rules/`.
- Other files: `tools/gen-classpath-26.sh`, `tools/fetch-import-deps.js`, `entrypoint.sh`, `package.json`, `run.sh`, `Dockerfile`.
- From `lib/`: `lib/cyrus/versions/registry.json` and `lib/cyrus/import/deps.json`.
- `toolchain.tgz` must already be in `/opt/modbuilder` on the VM. The script checks for it.

**The old hand-kept script was missing** 9 modules, 6 data files and `template/`. The image build would have failed, or silently used stale copies.

**JDK 25 / 26.x lane.** Run with `JDK25=yes`. That adds the pinned Temurin `25.0.4.1+1` and Gradle `9.8.1` build arguments, each sha256-verified, plus `MC26_PINS='26.2=26.2.build.133-stable 26.1.2=26.1.2.build.74-stable'`.

- Resolving the 26.x classpath does NOT make 26.x buildable. That is the registry's `buildable` flag (today `false` for 26.1.2, 26.2 and 26.3).
- Mark a 26.x version buildable only after this image is live and an eval has run.

**Health checks the script makes.**

- Before: the service is idle (`running:0`), and it records the running image tag for rollback.
- After:
  - `promptVersion` equals `prompts.js`.
  - `features.catalogTools:true` confirms the new image is the one running.
  - `release.scannerSha256` equals the sha256 of `scan.js`, so the hardened scan is live. On a mismatch the script rolls back.
  - `release.registrySha256` equals `registry.json`.
  - The `auth` field: `api_key` for a paid key; `subscription` or `subscription_login` for your login; `gateway_token`; or `none`. Before r28, the login-file mode wrongly reported `none`.

**Smoke.** The script sends one injection-style request that the guard must refuse (`errorCode: refused`). That is one Haiku guard call.

Afterwards, run `smoke-readonly.sh service`.

**Rollback.** Automatic on a failed build or health check. By hand:

```
ssh -J root@178.63.94.114 root@10.20.1.253 'cd /opt/modbuilder && tar xzf .backup-<ts>.tgz -C /opt/modbuilder && ./run.sh <previous image>'
```

The script prints the exact backup file name and the previous image.

## 4. Switch the build service from your subscription login to an API key
## 6. Switch features on: preview accounts first, the public last

Turn things on in this order, **one line at a time**. After each line:

1. Run `smoke-readonly.sh flags worker`.
2. Run one real build as a preview account.
3. Watch `journalctl -u nxeon-worker`.

**Rollback for every line:** set the flag back (`0`/unset or `false`), restart the same process, and run `smoke-readonly.sh flags`.

While `cyrus_studio_public_enabled` is off, only preview accounts can build at all. That is the safety net for this whole section.

| # | Switch (process) | Needs first | What it opens |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6.1 | `CYRUS_DESIGNER=1` (web) | step 3 | Item/ability, menu, quest, boss/encounter, HUD/glyph and motion designers. These are compiled into the jar and not plan-gated. |
| 6.2 | `CYRUS_ITEM_STATES=1` (web) | step 3, texture plan | Item model states (bow pull, gun aim, display contexts) |
| 6.3 | `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO=1`, then `CYRUS_WORLDGEN=1` (web) | step 3; a small paid trial of model-written specs | Data packs, then world generation. **A broken worldgen pack stops a server at its next start**, so worldgen delivery needs the orchestrator's rollback (6.8). |
| 6.4 | `CYRUS_CREATURES=1` (web + worker) | 5b (BetterModel), a 26.x version marked buildable after step 3 + eval | Animated creatures |

# 00 Overview: what Cyrus is

Cyrus is Nxeon's AI game-mod studio. A customer describes a mod in plain language (or edits it with studios and designers), and Cyrus produces a tested, installable artifact for their game server. Minecraft (Paper servers) is the one game that is built for real today. It is a product that sits inside Nxeon now and is designed to become its own product (cyrus.my) later.

> Status words used in all these docs: **live** (in production), **built** (merged into the integration branch `feature/cyrus-r2`, verified on node-2/dev host, NOT deployed), **pending** (on a branch not yet merged), **parked** (owner hold). **As of 2026-10-11 nothing from the r0..r40 programme is deployed, migrated in production, merged to `main` or switched on**, except the pre-programme Mod Builder / Cyrus v1-v6 studio that was deployed on 2026-10-08 with everything new gated off, and the static landing page at cyrus.my.

## The product in one page

- **Describe it, get a mod.** Prompt -> prompt check -> capability router -> build service (AI writes Java against a pinned Paper API) -> javac -> safety scan -> jar. Failed builds are repaired automatically (up to 3 times, cheap-first).
- **Studios** edit the same mod project without prompting: Texture, Sound, Model (viewport, paint, cuboid/bone editor, mesh retexture), Motion, Config and Stats, plus designers for items/abilities, menus, quests, bosses, encounters and HUDs.
- **Engine, not a prompt box.** A typed, versioned `ModSpec`, immutable revisions, reserved namespaces, deterministic generators, a real-server **Test Flight** (boot, RCON, playtest bots) and a delivery orchestrator with proven rollback.
- **Compose and import.** Conflict engine + Mod Packs (install and roll back as one unit), import your own mod source, data packs and worldgen.
- **Library.** A CC0-only, catalogued asset library (62k+ staged rows) with a contribution pipeline, filters and takedown.
- **Installs onto Nxeon game servers** through a scoped bridge (consent, per-server grants), or download the jar.
- **Community.** NxLabs mod pages, remixes, ratings, community-tested badge, pass-rate page.

## Plans and models

| Plan | Customer-facing model | What it unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| Free | (starter grant: one free build) | Builds only; no studios, no asset creation |
| **Katara** ($4.99/mo) | fast model (Haiku class) | Builds; no studios |
| **Saka** ($19.99/mo) | balanced model (Sonnet class) | + Sound Studio and Sound Library |
| **Yakko / "All models"** ($49.99/mo) | strongest model (Opus class) | + Texture Studio, Model Studio, Texture Library: everything |

# 01 Architecture

## Layers

```
 customer / staff browser
        |
 UI layer ......... app/dashboard/cyrus/** (studio v5/v6), app/**/cyrus* (r39 customer app), /admin/cyrus*, /cyrus (NXM landing),
        |            components/cyrus/**, lib/cyrus/{store,forge,fx,...} (client state + canvas engine)
 route layer ...... app/api/cyrus/**, app/api/mod-builder/**, app/api/admin/cyrus/**, app/api/cyrus/v1/** (API v1)
        |
 engine layer ..... lib/cyrus/** (game-agnostic core + per-feature modules, see reference/modules.md)
        |  \__ lib/cyrus/host (the HOST SEAM)  <-- the only door to Nxeon
        |
 worker layer ..... worker/ + lib/cyrus/worker/schedule.ts (ONE scheduler entry: registerCyrusSweeps)
        |
 build service .... services/modbuilder (Docker on VM 88001): Claude CLI -> javac -> scan -> jar
 flight hosts ..... node-2: Test Flight (throwaway Paper), meshgen/Blender sandbox, sound render, Try It controller
 data ............. Postgres (Cyrus* tables via cyrusDb), object stores (packs, library), staging disk /tank/cyrus-library-staging
```

Rule of the layers: pure modules (`lib/cyrus/**` marked "PURE, client-safe") hold schemas, validators, planners and simulators; anything that touches the network, disk, DB or a subprocess is "SERVER ONLY" and reached through injected dependencies, so the same logic runs in unit tests, on node-2 flights and in production.

## The host seam (direction A: Cyrus needs things FROM Nxeon)

`lib/cyrus/host/` defines small interfaces; inside Nxeon `host/nxeon.ts` answers them with the existing Nxeon code unchanged. Moving Cyrus out means giving it a different answer to the same interfaces (`host/http.ts`, an HTTP client for Nxeon's Platform API).

| Interface | What Cyrus asks for |
|---|---|
| `settings` | read/write Settings (`cyrus_*` keys), stored-value helpers |
| `rateLimit`, `audit` | rate limiting and the audit log |
| `auth` / `access` | current/real user, `requireArea`, `canAccess`, preview-account list |
| `users`, `jobs`, `servers`, `records` | platform tables Cyrus must not read directly (97 call sites to 0, enforced by tsc) |
| `installs` | engine install/uninstall of prefetched packages, state path, `openFiles` |
| `builds` (r34) | the build engine (`ModBuild` store) |
| `mods` (r34) | mod pages |
| `billing` (r34) | money: Stripe containment + wallet (default provider = Nxeon; an own-Stripe adapter is built but unused) |
| `db` | the typed `cyrusDb` accessor: only Cyrus' own tables + `$transaction`/raw SQL |

Ratchets (tests that stop the coupling growing): `test/cyrus-host-seam.test.ts` (Nxeon imports under `lib/cyrus`: 74 -> 40 -> **5**, all client-safe/pure and copied on move day), `test/cyrus-db-seam.test.ts` (no Nxeon-table access), `test/cyrus-db-split.test.ts` (Cyrus-table call sites outside `lib/cyrus` must use `cyrusDb`; r37 found 338, r43 is moving them). Detail and the move plan: [CYRUS-PLATFORM.md](../CYRUS-PLATFORM.md), [CYRUS-MOVE-RUNBOOK.md](../CYRUS-MOVE-RUNBOOK.md).

## The Nxeon <-> Cyrus bridge (both directions)

```
 Direction A: Cyrus -> Nxeon (host seam / Nxeon Platform API v1, served BY Nxeon)
   identity, wallet/Stripe, entitlement, list servers, inventory, write mod files (hash preconditions), reload/restart, logs, set pack
 Direction B: Nxeon -> Cyrus (Cyrus API v1 + signed webhooks, served BY Cyrus)
   projects, builds, catalog, installs, personal API keys; webhooks: build.finished, mod.published, install.result, ...
 Both sides: Ed25519 signed assertions with a STABLE subject id (never email), service tokens cyk_<id>_<secret> (only sha256 stored), idempotency keys, audit.
```

- **API v1** (`lib/cyrus/api/v1`, `app/api/cyrus/v1`, flag `CYRUS_API_V1`): OpenAPI 3.1 generated from the Zod schemas (`docs/api/cyrus-v1.openapi.yaml`, see [reference/openapi.md](reference/openapi.md)); read slice, 6 write endpoints, 5 signed webhooks with a transactional outbox, retries and dead letter. The Nxeon-side client and receiver are in `lib/cyrus-client` (imports nothing from `lib/cyrus`).
- **Platform API v1** (`lib/nxeon-platform`, flag `CYRUS_PLATFORM_API`): per-server **grants** a user gives Cyrus on a consent screen (`servers.read`, `inventory.read`, `files.write.mods`, `server.reload/restart`, `logs.read.tail`, `pack.set`), call audit, rate limits, hash-checked file changes; entitlement mirror (fail closed); Nxeon -> Cyrus events with an outbox (`server.version_changed`, `server.deleted`, `grant.revoked` ...).
- **Domain mode** (`CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE`, r36): one app serves `nxeon.cloud/dashboard/cyrus` (portal chrome) and `cyrus.my/...` (Cyrus chrome); Sign in with Nxeon / Sign in with Cyrus land on the same account; single logout both ways. Detail: [05 bridge and accounts](05-bridge-and-accounts.md).

## Target architecture and monorepo / deploy plan (r37, scaffold only)

```
 cyrus.my (landing, Cloudflare)    app.cyrus.my (customer app)     admin.cyrus.my (Cyrus admin)
              \                          |                         /
               +--- Cyrus services: API (api.cyrus.my) + workers + own DB + object storage/CDN + build service
                              |  ^
        Cyrus -> Nxeon:       |  |   Nxeon -> Cyrus:
        Nxeon Platform API    v  |   Cyrus API v1 + signed webhooks
                          nxeon.cloud (portal, billing, game servers, admin)
```

Principles: Nxeon = identity + money + game-server hosting; Cyrus = everything about mods; one account, one wallet, one Stripe; the browser talks straight to the service that owns a feature; every cross-app call is a versioned, tested contract; every phase flag-gated and reversible. Phases P0..P8 (decisions, front door, Cloudflare for Nxeon, extract the Cyrus app into a monorepo, bridge hardening, data split, portals, infra move, launch gate) are in the plan file `CYRUS-FULL-PLAN.md` (agent-notes, summarised in [12 gaps and roadmap](12-gaps-and-roadmap.md)).

Monorepo (r37): `platform/targets.json` + a generated dependency map (`docs/cyrus-platform-depmap.md`), `scripts/platform/affected.mjs`, `apps/cyrus-site` (the static landing with atomic publish/rollback), `scripts/ship <nxeon|cyrus|site|all>`, `scripts/promote-cyrus.sh` (dry-run capable, **not armed**). **No source file has been moved**; physical extraction into `apps/` is a later, single-agent job after the r38-r45 work merges.

## Data flow: a build

```
 prompt -> lib/cyrus/prompt-check (gibberish refused before tokens are held)
        -> lib/cyrus/route + engine-core/router (what artifact does this need? honest limits, plan gate, fail closed)
        -> tokens: reserve  (lib/cyrus/tokens, cost caps, kill switches)
        -> lib/modbuilder/create.ts createModBuild -> build service POST /builds (tier -> model, images, ModSpec, assets, designs, catalog tools)
              service: Claude CLI (Read/Write/Edit only) in a throwaway workspace -> precheck -> javac --release N vs pinned Paper API
                       -> autofix / repair (<=3, cheap-first, escalate after 2) -> bytecode+source scan -> jar (reproducible) -> release record
        -> portal: NDJSON follow stream (lib/cyrus/follow) -> studio shows live code; tokens: settle (or release on failure)
        -> optional: Test Flight gate (worker sweep) on node-2 -> verdict kept on the build; playtest bots
        -> install: delivery orchestrator (lib/cyrus/delivery) -> Mods engine -> GAME_MOD_SYNC job -> guest server (backup, staged write, rollback)
```

## Data flow: a studio edit

`studio UI -> lib/cyrus/<studio>/* pure core (validate, simulate) -> API route (session + plan gate + flag, fail closed) -> revision (immutable, 3-way merge into editor drafts) -> asset/pack builder -> next build or no-model designer build -> delivery`.

## Where to find things

- Directory map with each module's own header comment: [reference/modules.md](reference/modules.md).
- Routes: [reference/routes.md](reference/routes.md). Tables: [reference/db-tables.md](reference/db-tables.md). Flags: [reference/flags-and-env.md](reference/flags-and-env.md).
