### Cyrus token economy (2026-10-07, branch `feature/cyrus-tokens`)

Customers pay for Cyrus's AI in **Cyrus tokens**. Design and every number with its reasoning: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-economy/ECONOMY.md`. **Preview-only until launch:** Setting `cyrus_tok_live=false` means only private-preview accounts (`lib/preview-access.ts` "modbuilder") earn grants, see the checkout line, the balance or the plans. Everyone else sees and earns nothing (`lib/cyrus/tokens/access.ts tokensActiveFor`, fails closed). Cyrus is labelled **Beta · Minecraft Java only** wherever tokens appear.

**Unit.** 1 token = $0.002 of the build service's measured `costUsd` (`cyrus_tok_tokens_per_usd=500`), times a model multiplier (Katara 1, Saka 1, Yakko 1.25), min 5 per build that reached the AI. Typical builds: Katara ~34 tokens (ChunkMirror 80), Saka ~52 (complex ~95; Sonnet-5 tier builds 150-338), Yakko ~214 simple. Customers never see a USD figure per token or a model family name (`test/cyrus-tokens-economy.test.ts`).

**Where tokens come from.**
- **Game servers**: on purchase `clamp(round5(100 + 16 x monthly $), 150, 750)`, on every paid renewal `clamp(round5(25 + 6 x monthly $), 40, 300)`; monthly $ = what was actually paid per month. Prepaid N-month terms earn per month (cap 12). Lots expire after 90 days (or term + 30 d). $0 trial starts earn the initial grant on the first paid renewal. Idempotent `gs:<serverId>:initial` / `gs:<serverId>:renew:<periodStartISO>`. Abuse caps: 3 initial grants per account per 30 days, 3,000 unexpired server tokens held. **Only games Cyrus builds for earn** (and get the checkout line): the server's game family must be a `status: "live"` game in `lib/cyrus/games.ts` (`lib/cyrus/tokens/games.ts earnsC
- **Plans** (Stripe Billing subscriptions, monthly): Katara $4.99 = 750 tokens/month (Katara), Saka $19.99 = 3,500 (Katara, Saka), All models $49.99 = 10,000 (all three). Every paid invoice grants (`plan:<invoiceId>`), so renewals stack; each month's plan tokens last 3 months from their grant (`cyrus_tok_plan_rollover_months`), so at most 3 months stack. (A first design trimmed to "3 x the current plan" on each invoice; a real test-mode run showed a replayed old invoice could then expire paid tokens, so the cap is by age.) Upgrade = immediate proration (`always_invoice`, tokens in proportion to the money collected); downgrade = at the next renewal; cancel = at period end, plan tokens stay 30
- **Top-ups**: one-off Checkout payment, $5-$100, 120 tokens/$, 12-month expiry, no unlock (`topup:<sessionId>`).
- **Admin**: grant / revoke / comp a tier at `/admin/cyrus-tokens`.

**Models.** No plan = Katara only; Katara plan = Katara; Saka plan = Katara + Saka; All models = all three; admin comp can raise it. Enforced server-side in `POST /api/mod-builder/builds` (403 `model_locked`).

**Spending** (`lib/cyrus/tokens/builds.ts`, called from the build route and `lib/modbuilder/store.ts syncBuild`): before the `ModBuild` row exists, `gateBuild` resolves the model, checks the unlock and **holds** the high end of the estimate (or the whole balance if that still covers the typical cost; else 402 `insufficient_tokens`; daily cap 5,000 tokens, 1,000 for accounts younger than 7 days, 429 `daily_cap`). When the build turns terminal, `settleBuildTokens` spends the **actual** cost and releases the rest: succeeded / refused / cancelled pay actual, our-side failures are free (3 per rolling 7 days, then actual), never-started builds release everything. A cost above the balance is a writ

**Ledger** (`lib/cyrus/tokens/ledger.ts`, the only writer). Additive models: `CyrusTokenAccount` (locked `FOR UPDATE` by every operation; `balance`/`reserved` are caches), `CyrusTokenLot` (source, remaining, expiry; spends draw soonest-expiring first), `CyrusTokenLedger` (append-only, `idemKey` UNIQUE: grant / purchase / reserve / spend / release / refund / expire / revoke, with `source`, `sourceRef`, `buildId`, `balanceAfter`), `CyrusTokenReservation` (one hold per build), `CyrusPlan` (the subscription mirror; `tier` = paid entitlement from invoices, `priceTier` = what bills next). Due lots are expired inside every operation, and by the worker.

**Stripe** (`lib/cyrus/tokens/billing.ts`). Prices are found by lookup_key `cyrus_plan_<tier>_v1` (override ids: `cyrus_tok_price_*`); create them with `scripts/cyrus-tokens-stripe-setup.ts` (TEST mode; refuses a live key unless `CYRUS_STRIPE_ALLOW_LIVE=1 ... --live`). # 05 Bridge and accounts

How a Nxeon customer becomes a Cyrus user, how money and plans move, and how Cyrus touches a customer's game server. State: **built and tested on node-2 with fakes and real Test Flight servers; nothing deployed; every switch OFF** (see [reference/flags-and-env.md](reference/flags-and-env.md), launch order in [07 operations](07-operations.md)).

## Today (inside Nxeon) vs the target
Today Cyrus uses Nxeon's sign-in, wallet, Stripe and game-server install path directly (through the host seam, [01 architecture](01-architecture.md)). The target (owner decisions 2026-10-11, defaults from the full plan): **Nxeon is the identity provider and the only money system; Cyrus sells nothing itself**; per-server scoped grants, never SSH credentials; a separate Cyrus Postgres; Cyrus has its own admin; separate Cyrus Terms/Privacy (lawyer-reviewed before public launch). The owner has confirmed these as the working defaults; the open exceptions are in [12 gaps and roadmap](12-gaps-and-roadmap.md).

## SSO and identity (r36, `CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE`)
One app serves both hosts. `lib/cyrus/bridge/{config,routing}.ts` + middleware: cyrus.my gets the Cyrus brand bar around the same `/dashboard/cyrus` pages; the customer-app tree is exposed as `/home`, `/new`, `/account`, `/projects[/<id>]`; portal pages hand off to Nxeon; everything else 404s. **Sign in with Nxeon** = redirect with an Ed25519 signed assertion (state/nonce bound to the starting browser, single-use jti, exact `redirect_uri`, 120 s), a stable **subject id (Nxeon user id; never email)**, verified email required, a separate Cyrus cookie parented to the Nxeon session; **Sign in with Cyrus** on Nxeon lands on the same account; sign-up goes through Nxeon `/register` behind a consent screen; impersonation never crosses hosts; logout is a signed hop both ways. Keys: `CYRUS_BRIDGE_*` (secrets, env only). Routes under `/cyrus-host/*` (sign-in, sign-up, auth start/callback/handoff/logout).
Verified: two-origin e2e 46/46 with the mode on and 6/6 off (no studio on cyrus.my, no IdP, internal tree 404, spoofed marker ignored); own-flow security review (open redirect, login CSRF, replay, forged subject, header spoofing, impersonation leak, fixation, consent/logout CSRF). Not run: `next build`, a real browser, staging behind nginx.

## Wallet, tokens and plans
- **Unit and sources**: see [00 overview](00-overview.md). 1 token = $0.002 of measured AI cost (`cyrus_tok_tokens_per_usd=500`), Yakko x1.25, min 5 per build. Game-server purchase grants `clamp(round5(100 + 16 x monthly $), 150, 750)`; each paid renewal `clamp(round5(25 + 6 x monthly $), 40, 300)` (only for games Cyrus builds for); lots expire after 90 days; plans Katara $4.99 = 750/month, Saka $19.99 = 3,500, All models $49.99 = 10,000, stacking, each month's tokens last 3 months; top-ups $5-$100 at 120 tokens/$, 12-month expiry. Placeholder amounts for the r41 "free tokens with deploys and renewals" copy are pending the owner.
- **Ledger**: append-only, idempotent (`idemKey` UNIQUE), reserve -> settle -> release per build; tables `CyrusTokenAccount/Lot/Ledger/Reservation`, `CyrusPlan`; the only writer is `lib/cyrus/tokens/ledger.ts`. Our-side failures are free (3 per rolling 7 days). Daily caps (5,000 tokens; 1,000 for accounts under 7 days). Sweep every 5 minutes.
- **Stripe**: plan prices found by lookup key `cyrus_plan_<tier>_v1` (`scripts/cyrus-tokens-stripe-setup.ts`, TEST mode; refuses a live key without an explicit override). Cyrus checkout sessions carry `cyrusUserId`, never the Nxeon user id, so Nxeon's wallet engine can never treat them as a top-up (pinned by a test).
- **Starter grant**: ONE free build (`cyrus_tok_starter=70`), with a guard against split launch flags.
- **Launch pair**: `cyrus_studio_public_enabled` and `cyrus_tok_live` must move TOGETHER (a public studio without the economy builds for free; the economy without the studio sells nothing). `lib/cyrus/launch-state.ts` refuses a split pair; the admin Flags tab flips both with a typed confirm.
- **Purchases from either host (r36)**: card checkouts return to the host they started on; wallet top-ups (`CYRUS_WALLET_PAY`) are idempotent by reference with a compensating refund and pending/failed states; signed purchase webhooks (`CYRUS_PURCHASE_EVENTS*`) credit tokens once; refunds and chargebacks reverse unspent tokens once (`CYRUS_CHARGEBACK_REVERSAL`). Gap: no wallet button in the tokens modal (API only), and card purchases credit directly rather than through the event path.

## Entitlement sync (r38)
Plans and tokens are Nxeon products; `GET /api/platform/cyrus/v1/entitlements` plus a signed `entitlement.changed` event feed Cyrus's **mirror** (`CYRUS_ENTITLEMENT_MIRROR`, 60 s cache, `CYRUS_ENTITLEMENT_MAX_AGE_H`), **fail closed** when unknown; reconciliation job; refunds/chargebacks reverse once; a partner-attribution hook (`CYRUS_PARTNER_ATTRIBUTION`) computes a proposal only (whether the Creator Partner Program 50%/10% applies to Cyrus plans is an open decision).

## Platform API and per-server grants (r38)
- **Connect Cyrus** consent screen `/dashboard/connect/cyrus`: a user ticks which servers Cyrus may act on. 7 scopes (servers.read, inventory.read, files.write.mods, server.reload, server.restart (budgeted), logs.read.tail, pack.set), revocable any time; every call tied to user + server + grant; stores memory + SQL (`CYRUS_SERVER_GRANTS`, `CYRUS_SERVER_GRANTS_STORE`; SQL proposal `prisma/manual-migration-cyrus-bridge-grants.sql`, not applied).
- **Platform API v1** `/api/platform/cyrus/v1/*` (served by Nxeon, `CYRUS_PLATFORM_API`): servers, inventory (incl. Mods-tab records), file primitives (allow-listed paths, 64 MiB caps, sha preconditions), reload, budgeted restart, log tail, pack.set; HMAC service key (`CYRUS_PLATFORM_KEYS`) + Cyrus-signed Ed25519 user assertion + grant per call; rate limits, idempotency, audit; a **rollback-only window after revoke**. Cyrus consumes it via `createHttpHost({ platform })` and the delivery orchestrator runs over the primitives. Contract: [reference/openapi.md](reference/openapi.md).
- **Events Nxeon -> Cyrus** (`CYRUS_PLATFORM_EVENTS*`, signed outbox, change watcher): `server.version_changed` (marks mods outdated), `server.deleted` (revokes grants), `server.restarted`, `grant.created/updated/revoked`. **Events Cyrus -> Nxeon** (API v1 webhooks): `build.finished`, `mod.published`, `install.result`, `delivery.rolledback` and entitlement-related ones; outbox with retries 1 m, 5 m, 30 m, 2 h, 12 h, then dead letter (kept for replay).
- **UX**: "Create a mod for this server" button (`CYRUS_SERVER_BUTTON`) prefilling game, version, loader; pre-install conflict report (Mods-tab duplicates block) in the install modal.
- Verified: DB tests 12/12 on a throwaway DB; two-service e2e 5/5 (fresh install, revoke mid-install, revoke mid-update, broken worldgen rollback with 2 budgeted restarts, no/read-only grant); a **real node-2 run** delivered through 120 API calls and booted a real Paper 1.21.11 Test Flight (passed) and restored exact bytes after a revoke mid-update (the first run found and fixed a rollback bug). Not done: no real Nxeon server touched; memory stores per process; `library.contributed` unemitted; card top-ups not in the entitlement snapshot.

## Cyrus API v1 (direction B)
Versioned, token-authenticated API for Nxeon or any trusted site (`CYRUS_API_V1`, off = 404; bad config = 503, never "no auth"): service tokens `cyk_<id>_<secret>` (only sha256 stored, scopes, per-key rpm), **Ed25519 subject assertions** (Cyrus holds only the public key; `iss`=client, `aud`, 120 s, single-use jti, email refused), identity-clients rule (`CYRUS_API_V1_IDENTITY_CLIENTS`, default `nxeon`; r32 AC-1), idempotency keys and `CyrusApiIdempotency`, errors/pagination/versioning per [../api/CYRUS-API-PLAN.md](../api/CYRUS-API-PLAN.md). Operations (live vs planned): [reference/openapi.md](reference/openapi.md). r44 adds personal API keys (`cyk_...`) accepted by v1. Nxeon-side client: `lib/cyrus-client`.

## Webhooks and domain mode
Webhooks Cyrus -> Nxeon: `CYRUS_API_V1_WEBHOOKS` + `_URL` + a dedicated `_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (24+ chars, never `AUTH_SECRET`); nothing in product code emits them until the flags are on, except the four emitters r38 wired. Domain mode and hosts: `CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE`, `CYRUS_HOSTS`, `CYRUS_ORIGIN`; cyrus.my/app/admin/api subdomain DNS and nginx are owner actions (runbook).

## Gaps (honest)
Nxeon does not yet serve the host API in production; write endpoints not exercised over real HTTP across machines; no collector for telemetry; SQL outbox dispatcher and conversion sender not built; attribution receiver on nxeon.cloud not built; Kodely identity policy and networking mods in packs are owner decisions. Move-day plan: [CYRUS-MOVE-RUNBOOK.md](../CYRUS-MOVE-RUNBOOK.md).

Gate fails closed on every page and action (switch + studio gate + preview gate); Cyrus tables only via `cyrusDb`. Not run: `next build`, cyrus.my host mode in a real browser, real installs, notices actually sent. Personal API keys became accepted by API v1 in r44 (pending merge). Open owner request (r41, pending): Cyrus opens full screen from the Nxeon top-bar button with a small "Back to Nxeon" widget, the Cyrus credit chip is removed from Nxeon's top bar, the button restyled, new plan SVGs, live token spend during builds with totals per mod/revision.

## The v5/v6 studio (`/dashboard/cyrus`, deployed to preview 2026-10-08)
The owner's own redesign (handoff `/tank/handoffs/cyrus/cyrus-handoff/`): forge canvas (Cyrus core -> games -> categories -> mods), composer with model picker and estimate, inspector (Code / Explain / Versions / Files / Notes), live code streaming from the build service, switcher with projects per game, token chip. ## Public pages
- `/cyrus` marketing page (NXM generated page: edit `tools/nxm/native/cyrus/{body.html,page.css,page.js}` then `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py cyrus`; never hand-edit `app/nxm/_pages/cyrus`): 404 + noindex + out of the sitemap until setting `cyrus_public_enabled`; dark mode only by owner decision.
- `/mods/cyrus` and NxLabs mod pages (`lib/cyrus-mods`, switch `cyrus_mods_public_enabled`): community listings, remixes, forks, ratings, library, community-tested laurel, SEO from the generated doc only. `/mods/cyrus/pass-rates` (flag `cyrus_passrate_enabled`): measured per-version pass rates; empty state until an accepted eval baseline exists.
- **cyrus.my landing** (static, `apps/cyrus-site`, atomic publish + rollback): v7 LIVE since 2026-10-11 (black/white + electric blue/violet, Cyrus Core hero, interactive studio cards, Katara/Saka/Yakko animated SVG icons, Nxeon bridge section). The updated landing (8 real-time three.js effect scenes on one shared renderer, better 3D models) is in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/v7-landing/`, built and shot, **NOT published; waiting on the owner** (keep a backup of the live page). Plans-section copy is added from r41's report.

## Admin (r40 and earlier, `/admin/cyrus*`)
Seven role-gated tabs from v6 (overview/health, builds, users and tokens, games and models, community moderation, library and safety, audit log) plus r40: **spend vs revenue** and Test Flight/eval/error panels; read-only **view-as** (audited 30-minute grant; impersonation is refused); ban with optional ADMIN-only Nxeon suspension; GDPR export + fail-closed erasure plan (`CYRUS_GDPR_ERASE`); **library moderation** (decisions, near-dupes, stats, filter-list editor, DMCA case log); **Flags and kill switches** (launch-pair guard with typed confirm, global build pause, AI gateway kill, every switch, env flags read-only, history); **Cost** (per model/account, caps default off and fail closed when set, margin per plan, anomalies); **Reconciliation** (wallet vs tokens, ledger invariants, plan drift, dead webhook replay); notification admin. Also `/admin/cyrus-tokens` (liability, holds, spend vs cost, plans/MRR, grant/revoke/comp), `/admin/cyrus-mods`, `/admin/mod-builder`. Audit rows go to the existing `AuditLog` with before/after. Not built: a read-only Cyrus card on the main Nxeon admin; admin.cyrus.my split.

## Notifications (r40, `CYRUS_NOTIFY`, `CYRUS_NOTIFY_EMAIL`)
One system (`lib/cyrus/notify`): in-app bell, preference center, five events wired (build finished, install result, mod outdated, takedown, ...), cyrus.my email through Nxeon's mailer via the optional `host.mail`; SPF/DKIM/DMARC checklist for the new sender domain in the docs. Tables `CyrusNotification`, `CyrusNotificationPref` (SQL not applied). The bell, consent banner and preference center were not screenshotted (flags off); no real email sent.

## Support (r40)
Tickets stay in Nxeon. A ticket opened with `/dashboard/support?cyrusBuild=<id>` carries a snapshot of the build (spec, flight record, errors; table `CyrusTicketContext`) and the admin ticket view shows a Cyrus panel; staff can view-as read-only. Customer "Get help" link on the build page is URL-contract only.

## Analytics and consent (r40, `CYRUS_CONSENT`, `CYRUS_ATTRIBUTION`)
Cookie-consent banner for cyrus.my (React + a static `consent.js` for the landing), consent-gated privacy-safe attribution/referral capture, and a spec for Meta/Google conversion payloads. Not built: conversion sender, attribution receiver on nxeon.cloud. Telemetry privacy wording needs a lawyer.

# AC - Cyrus launch-hardening security audit (r32, 2026-10-11)
Branch `feature/cyrus-r32-security` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r32`, from `feature/cyrus-r2` @ 92d7fa4a69). Nothing deployed, migrated or switched on.
Method: read-only adversarial pass over everything Cyrus exposes (4 parallel readers + one real Blender probe on node-2), then fixes with tests.
# BUILD HOST — all builds and heavy dev work run on node-2, not the primary

**Since 2026-10-07 (owner decision).** The primary (ns5002569, 51.79.162.96) only serves the live site:
prod web/worker, Postgres, customer VMs. Parallel agent builds there pushed load to 16+, filled swap
and hard-crashed it on 2026-10-06. Everything heavy now runs on **node-2 = nxeon-fsn1
(178.63.94.114)**, inside a capped systemd slice.

Full technical write-up: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` → "Build host (node-2)".

## What runs where

| Work | Where | How |
|---|---|---|
| Production / staging release builds (`npm install`, `prisma generate`, `next build`) | node-2, `nxeon-build-prod.slice` | automatically by `scripts/promote-production.sh` / `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` |
| Schema push, pre-cutover smoke (:3095), cutover, restarts, rollback | primary | same scripts, unchanged |
| Agent `tsc`, tests, `next build`, `next dev`, Playwright, throwaway DBs | node-2, `nxeon-build-agents.slice` | `scripts/devhost` (below) |
| Editing files, git commits | primary, in **your own worktree** | as before |

## Caps on node-2 (it also runs ~13 customer VMs — never touch them)

- `nxeon.slice` CPUWeight 20 / IOWeight 10 (VMs in `qemu.slice` win any contention ~5:1)
- `nxeon-build.slice`: **CPUQuota 900 % (9 of 12 threads, raised 2026-10-08), MemoryMax 10 G, MemoryHigh 9.5 G, no swap**
  - `nxeon-build-prod.slice`: release builds — CPUWeight 1000, MemoryLow 6 G, oom_score_adj 500
  - `nxeon-build-agents.slice`: agent work — **MemoryMax 7 G**, oom_score_adj 1000 (dies first)
- every process: nice 10, ionice best-effort 7. Build files live on `tank` (separate SATA SSD);
  VMs are on `rpool` (NVMe), so build IO never hits their disks.
- **Build lock** on node-2: `/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock` — one heavy job at a time
  (release builds, `devhost build|test`, `devhost run --lock`). Locked agent jobs are capped at
  25 min by default so a promote (waits max 30 min) is never starved.

## How agents work from now on

1. Make your own worktree on the primary (never work in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`):
   `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main`
   You do NOT need `node_modules` in it (and never symlink one in).
2. Edit with your normal tools. Then, from inside the worktree, run heavy things on node-2:
   ```
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tsc                    # npx tsc --noEmit
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost test [test/x.test.ts]  # tsx --test (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost build                  # next build (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- <cmd...>        # anything else; add --lock if heavy
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost db push                # schema into YOUR throwaway DB
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost dev                    # next dev on node-2 127.0.0.1:<port>
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tunnel <port>          # reach it from the primary (curl/Playwright)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- npx playwright test ...   # or run Playwright ON node-2
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost pull <path> [dest]     # copy screenshots/reports back
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost stop [name|all]        # ALWAYS stop dev servers when done
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost rm                     # when finished: units, DB and node-2 copy gone
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost status                 # node-2 load, slice memory, lock, running units
   ```
   Each command mirrors your worktree's source (git-tracked + untracked-not-ignored; never
   `.git`, `node_modules`, `.next`, `.env*`) to `/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>` on node-2, installs
   deps there when `package-lock.json`/schema changed, and runs the command in the agents slice.
   The node-2 copy is disposable — commit in your primary worktree only.
3. **Throwaway database**: every workspace gets its own `wt_<name>` on node-2's private Postgres
   cluster (`127.0.0.1:5433`, role `nxeon_agent`, never exposed). `DATABASE_URL`, a random
   `AUTH_SECRET`, `APP_URL`, `PORT` are preset. Extra non-secret env: `devhost env set K=V` (it
   refuses any value that is a live prod/staging value). **Agents never need, and must never use,
   production DB credentials.**
4. Only if node-2 is down: say so to the owner. Do not fall back to building on the primary.

# 07 Operations

Authoritative step lists live in the repo runbooks: [CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK.md](../CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK.md) (owner, step by step), [CYRUS-MOVE-RUNBOOK.md](../CYRUS-MOVE-RUNBOOK.md) (move day, draft), [CYRUS-PLATFORM.md](../CYRUS-PLATFORM.md) (monorepo, ship, Cloudflare, data split, observability). This page is the summary, the infrastructure map and the incident playbooks. **Agents never deploy, run production migrations, flip flags or touch VM 88001 or customer servers; the owner does (classifier blocks prod deploys for agents).** Secrets are never in these docs: this page names where they live.

## Where things run
| Place | What | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Primary** (ns5002569, OVH, Singapore) | production web (`nxeon-web`), worker (`nxeon-worker`), Postgres, nginx, customer VMs, `cyrus.my` static site | Serves live customers. Never build, test or run agent work here. Root disk has about 11 GB free: never write there. |
| **node-2** (nxeon-fsn1, Germany) | the BUILD HOST: release builds, all agent dev work (`scripts/devhost`), Test Flight, meshgen/Blender sandbox, sound render, Try It controller, throwaway Postgres (port 5433) | Also runs about 13 customer VMs (never touch). Caps: slice `nxeon-build.slice` (CPUQuota 900%), agents slice memory raised 2026-10-10 to **10 GB** and the build slice to **13 GB** (older text in `/root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md` says 7/10 GB); nice 10; **one heavy job at a time** via the lock `/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock`; locked agent jobs capped at 25 min. |
| **VM 88001** (Docker, inside the Nxeon network) | the build service image `modbuilder:<tag>` (Claude CLI + JDKs + classpaths) | Reached through the primary with a jump host. Running tag per last deploy: 0.4. Deploy only with `scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh` (derived from the Dockerfile, hash-checked, auto-rollback; `--list` first). |
| **Tank** (`/tank`) | one 3.6 TB spinning disk, NO redundancy: backups (689 GB), NX Labs mirror (150 GB quota), library staging, uploads, dev worktrees | Give the library its own dataset with a quota; keep a second copy of the proprietary SFX (owner OK pending). The NVMe pool is for customer VMs only. |
| Cloudflare | zone `cyrus.my` ACTIVE: apex + www proxied, served by nginx on the primary (`/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/cyrus-my`, root `/var/www/cyrus.my`); Nxeon zones NOT proxied yet | The Cloudflare API token that issued the certificate was pasted in chat once: **rotate it** (owner action). The token file path is `/root/.secrets/cloudflare-cyrus.ini` (root-only; never print). It cannot edit zone SSL settings: set SSL/TLS to **Full (strict)** in the dashboard. |

### cyrus.my hosting and the certificate watcher
Landing is a static site published atomically from `apps/cyrus-site` (`publish.sh`: release dirs, symlink swap, health check, auto-rollback, dry run unless `--go`; legacy dir kept as rollback). The Let's Encrypt certificate (DNS-01 via Cloudflare) was issued by the watcher `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-my-finish.sh` (log `cyrus-my-finish.log`: "cyrus.my now uses the Let's Encrypt cert"). Renewal is certbot's timer; check it after any nginx change. DNS for `app.`, `admin.`, `api.` subdomains and the nginx proxy paths are not done (owner list in OWNER-ACTIONS "r36").

## Deploy runbook (summary of the 8 steps, owner executes, one at a time, smoke after each)
Hazards first: never build or edit in `/opt/nxeon` (a raw build + restart caused two outages on 2026-10-01); check `uptime` first (the promote cutover rolls itself back on an overloaded primary); after stopping staging promote needs `--skip-staging-check`; never `pkill -f`; the 100+ commit branch is merged to `main` through a reviewed PR; every feature is OFF so landing the code changes nothing.
1. **Database**: additive manual SQL by hand, then check (`prisma/manual-migrations/*cyrus*.sql`, listed in [reference/db-tables.md](reference/db-tables.md); engine core has a trigger that must be run by hand; `scripts/cyrus-seed-managed-plugins.ts` after managed plugins).
2. **Code to production** with all switches off: `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>`, look at it, then `scripts/promote-production.sh`.
3. **Rebuild the build-service image on VM 88001** (`deploy-modbuilder.sh`, `JDK25=yes` for the 26.x lane; verifies `promptVersion`, `features.catalogTools`, `release.scannerSha256` = sha256 of `scan.js`, `release.registrySha256`; sends one injection-style request that must be refused).
4. **Switch the build service from the subscription login to an API key** before ANY public launch (`/health` field `auth` must read `api_key`; subscription login cannot power a public service).
5. **Infrastructure the switches depend on**: pack storage + public base, Pack Loader jar, BetterModel (managed plugin), node-2 Test Flight, sound render path, Blender, catalog index.
6. **Switch features on**, preview accounts first, one line at a time (designer, item states, data pack then worldgen, creatures, studios settings, import, Test Flight gate then block-on-fail, managed plugins then delivery, Mod Packs, sound library cleared, catalog tools, pass-rate page ...): see the table in the runbook; rollback = set the flag back and restart the same process.
7. **Public launch**: the pair `cyrus_studio_public_enabled` + `cyrus_tok_live` together, last (`FLIP=yes bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh` refuses unless `auth=api_key`). Rollback: set both false (settings are read on every request, immediate).
8. **Verification jobs** (no deploy needed): eval run, real-client test day.
Read-only smoke: `scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh [all|migrations|service|worker|flags|packs|delivery]` (no writes, no restarts, no model calls, never prints a secret; exits 1 on FAIL).

## Flags, settings and env
Full generated registry: [reference/flags-and-env.md](reference/flags-and-env.md) (about 320 names with default, where read, meaning). Structure: **env flags** `CYRUS_*` (web/worker/scripts; changing one needs an env edit + restart), **service env** `MB_*` (build service run.sh), **Settings** `cyrus_*` (DB, admin Flags tab, read every request, instant), plus the admin settings catalog (`lib/cyrus/admin/settings-catalog.ts`). Kill switches (instant, fail closed): `cyrus_builds_paused` (global build pause), AI gateway kill, `cyrus_mod_networking_enabled`, the launch pair. Helper to flip a setting by hand: `/root/agent-notes/set-setting.sh <key> <value>` (owner).

## Build lock, memory and load
One heavy job at a time on node-2 (builds, `devhost test|build|run --lock`). Many agents queue; weekly model usage is the other limit. node-2's agent slice has OOM-killed `next dev` (5+ GB) several times: run screenshots in batches and restart. Always `devhost stop all` and `devhost rm` when finished. Fixtures that import `lib/auth` need `scripts/cyrus/server-only-shim.cjs`.

## Observability and backups (r37, built, NOT installed)
`GET /api/cyrus/health` (names the release commit via `CYRUS_RELEASE_COMMIT`), error hook (`CYRUS_ERROR_WEBHOOK_URL`, scrubbed, deduplicated Discord), cost export (`scripts/cyrus/cost-export.sh`), alert rules and checker (`scripts/cyrus/alert-check.sh`, `deploy/cyrus/cyrus-alerts.service`, spend alert `CYRUS_SPEND_ALERT_USD`), uptime list and status-page spec, nightly **encrypted** backup (`scripts/cyrus/backup-nightly.sh`, public-key encryption, remote target, library files opt-in, SFX only encrypted; keys not in the repo). Cyrus has no backups of its own tables beyond Nxeon's Postgres backups until the data split; the proprietary SFX library has a single copy.

## Cloudflare for the Nxeon zones (groundwork only)
`deploy/cloudflare/` + `scripts/cloudflare/`: real client IP restored from `CF-Connecting-IP` only from Cloudflare ranges (generated nginx config, weekly updater, throwaway-nginx simulation 6/6), three first-hop X-Forwarded-For call sites fixed, static-only cache rules, websocket keepalive, origin certs. Keep game, mail, SSH and panel records grey (DNS only); keep `NXEON_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=1`. **Blocker**: Nxeon's terminal and console WebSocket servers send no pings, so Cloudflare would drop idle sessions after about 100 s. Nothing here is applied.

## Incident playbooks (past outages and how not to repeat them)
| Incident | Cause | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Two prod outages 2026-10-01 | raw `npm run build` + restart in the live tree | Deploy only via deploy-staging -> promote-production; builds run on node-2. |

# 08 Security

Full audit text: [CYRUS-SECURITY-AUDIT.md](../CYRUS-SECURITY-AUDIT.md) (r32, 2026-10-11; read-only adversarial pass by 4 readers plus a real Blender probe on node-2, then fixes with tests). **Result: no HIGH finding** (no cross-tenant read/write, no unauthenticated route, no raw proprietary sound served, no SSRF, no secrets in logs). Labels used there: VERIFIED-TEST (a test fails on the old code), VERIFIED-RUN (reproduced on real software), VERIFIED-READ (concrete trace), UNVERIFIED.

## Threat model (what Cyrus defends against)
| Asset | Threat | Main controls |
|---|---|---|
| Customer game servers | a malicious or buggy generated/imported mod; a leaked key writing to servers | bytecode + source **scan** (strict profile for generated, attested profile for imports, never called "safe"), no network for the build model, per-server **grants** with scopes, hash preconditions, rollback-only window after revoke, Test Flight boot before install, Mod Pack networking-consent gate |
| Build service / VM 88001 | prompt injection (incl. instructions inside images), code escaping the workspace | Read/Write/Edit-only tools in a throwaway workspace, prompt guard (`MB_GUARD`), path allow-list on diffs, injected text only as quoted data, refusal smoke request on every deploy |
| Money and tokens | free builds, double credit, replayed webhooks | append-only idempotent ledger, reserve/settle/release, launch-pair guard, HMAC + dedicated webhook secret, chargeback reversal once, daily caps, cost caps (default off) |
| Identity | forged subject, open redirect, CSRF, replay, impersonation leak | Ed25519 assertions with single-use jti, exact redirect_uri, nonce bound to the browser, stable subject id (never email), identity-clients allowlist |
| Library / legal | copyright/trademark content, takedown abuse, raw proprietary audio | CC0-only ingest, filters + hold queue, near-dup dedupe, takedown marks dependents, signed viewer-scoped URLs, raw audio never served |
| Blender / meshgen | arbitrary Python | template and parts-kit rungs first, AST guard on scratch scripts, transient systemd sandbox (no network, nobody, read-only fs, caps); scratch scripts stay OFF until a microVM exists |
| Data | GDPR, secrets | export + fail-closed erasure plan, scrubbed error hook, secrets only in env files / `/root/.secrets`, never in git or docs |

## Rules that never relax
Fail closed on unknown state (tokens, entitlements, plan, flags). Real servers only through Test Flight; never a customer server. Sound audio never in git or served raw. Game-derived material never public. No secret in docs, logs or briefs: reference the location only. Never deploy, migrate, flip flags or touch VM 88001 without the owner. Keep the host key (full trust for reads) on Nxeon only and rotate on move day.

## r32 findings: fixed (all with tests)
| # | Sev | Area | Finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AC-1 | MED | API v1 | a client with its own subject key could sign `sub=<any Nxeon user id>` | `CYRUS_API_V1_IDENTITY_CLIENTS` (default `nxeon`); others get 403 `subject_not_allowed` |
| AC-2 | MED | meshgen scratch | driver expressions bypassed the static scan and reached Blender's eval (proven on node-2) | scan covers driver expressions; scratch remains OFF |
| AC-3 | MED | designer Java | Javadoc/unicode-escape injection through names | `javadocText()` sanitises; also config exporter |
| AC-4 | MED | Mod Packs | pack create/install skipped networking consent and the Test Flight gate | `memberInstallGate()` on create, conflicts and every install |
| AC-5 | MED | library reports | one account could mass-hold assets with copyright reports | 5 legal auto-holds per reporter per 24 h, then 3 reporters needed |
| AC-6 | LOW-MED | library takedown | stored near-copies stayed published | takedown holds every published `duplicateOf` copy |
| AC-7 | MED (latent) | host HTTP server | a leaked host key could write any platform setting; body buffered before size check | writes limited to `cyrus_` keys; oversize refused before reading |
| AC-8 | LOW | Test Flight | `\r` not stripped in `server.properties` values | strip CR, LF, NUL, U+2028/2029/0085 |
| AC-9 | LOW | data packs | a command ending in `\` joins the next entry (1.20.2+) | refused (`line_continuation`) |

## r32 findings: open (status as of the last update)
| # | Sev | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| O-1 | LOW | telemetry ingest: HMAC over body only, no timestamp/nonce, whole body buffered | **closed in r40** (telemetry v2: timestamp + single-use batch, capped stream, IP limit) |
| O-2 | LOW | AI gateway tokens never expire | **closed in r40** (max age) |
| O-3 | LOW | Server Doctor audit-row failures swallowed | open (owner: fail closed or alert) |
| O-4 | LOW | Test Flight log-matcher regexes can backtrack | open (bounded by the runner's kill timeout; RE2 later) |
| O-5 | LOW | pack install/uninstall loop could restart a user's own server about once a minute; in-memory limiter | open (per-server restart budget N/hour is an owner number) |
| O-6 | LOW | no per-user Mod Pack count/byte quota; no create idempotency | open (owner: quota numbers) |
| O-7 | INFO | delivery Idempotency-Key not bound to the body | open (hash body into key) |
| O-8 | LOW | library filters are text-only (no NFKC/confusables, no pixel/audio classifier) | open (hold first-time contributors for review, or a classifier) |
| O-9 | LOW | import licence claim accepted as typed | open (manual review before any public share; public sharing is hard-off) |
| O-10 | INFO | hosted packs are public by sha1 (capability URL, no expiry) | open (owner: OK as public or signed URLs) |
| O-11 | LOW | API v1 replay caches are in-process (50k cap) | open (shared store before more than one instance) |
| O-12 | INFO | the host key is full trust for reads | by design |
| O-13 | - | meshgen kernel-escape untested | open (microVM/gVisor before `CYRUS_MESHGEN_SCRATCH`) |

Not read end to end by the audit: Test Flight `runner.js`, playtest `bot.js`, `telemetry/collect.ts`, library `stage-b/c.ts`, admin library routes. Later features (r36 SSO has its own review; r38 Platform API; r40 admin) were reviewed by their authors, not by an independent audit: **a second audit pass after r41-r45 and before launch is recommended** ([12 gaps and roadmap](12-gaps-and-roadmap.md)).

## Owner security decisions pending (from the r32 list)
Kodely identity policy for API v1; whether networking mods may be bundled into packs; copyright-report rules; per-server restart budget; Mod Pack quotas; build service must leave the subscription login for an API key with hard spend caps before public launch; rotate the Cloudflare token that was pasted in chat.
E

# 09 Testing and verification

The programme's rule: **evidence over claims**. A feature is "built" when its tests pass and a node-2 run exists, "verified" only for what a real run proved, and never "supported" without a real client or a real model build. This page says what exists and what does not.

| Money and tokens | free builds, double credit, replayed webhooks | append-only idempotent ledger, reserve/settle/release, launch-pair guard, HMAC + dedicated webhook secret, chargeback reversal once, daily caps, cost caps (default off) |
| Identity | forged subject, open redirect, CSRF, replay, impersonation leak | Ed25519 assertions with single-use jti, exact redirect_uri, nonce bound to the browser, stable subject id (never email), identity-clients allowlist |
| Library / legal | copyright/trademark content, takedown abuse, raw proprietary audio | CC0-only ingest, filters + hold queue, near-dup dedupe, takedown marks dependents, signed viewer-scoped URLs, raw audio never served |
| Blender / meshgen | arbitrary Python | template and parts-kit rungs first, AST guard on scratch scripts, transient systemd sandbox (no network, nobody, read-only fs, caps); scratch scripts stay OFF until a microVM exists |
| Data | GDPR, secrets | export + fail-closed erasure plan, scrubbed error hook, secrets only in env files / `/root/.secrets`, never in git or docs |

## Rules that never relax
Fail closed on unknown state (tokens, entitlements, plan, flags). Real servers only through Test Flight; never a customer server. Sound audio never in git or served raw. Game-derived material never public. No secret in docs, logs or briefs: reference the location only. Never deploy, migrate, flip flags or touch VM 88001 without the owner. Keep the host key (full trust for reads) on Nxeon only and rotate on move day.

| # | Sev | Area | Finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AC-1 | MED | API v1 | a client with its own subject key could sign `sub=<any Nxeon user id>` | `CYRUS_API_V1_IDENTITY_CLIENTS` (default `nxeon`); others get 403 `subject_not_allowed` |
| AC-2 | MED | meshgen scratch | driver expressions bypassed the static scan and reached Blender's eval (proven on node-2) | scan covers driver expressions; scratch remains OFF |
| AC-3 | MED | designer Java | Javadoc/unicode-escape injection through names | `javadocText()` sanitises; also config exporter |
| AC-4 | MED | Mod Packs | pack create/install skipped networking consent and the Test Flight gate | `memberInstallGate()` on create, conflicts and every install |
| AC-5 | MED | library reports | one account could mass-hold assets with copyright reports | 5 legal auto-holds per reporter per 24 h, then 3 reporters needed |
| AC-6 | LOW-MED | library takedown | stored near-copies stayed published | takedown holds every published `duplicateOf` copy |
| AC-7 | MED (latent) | host HTTP server | a leaked host key could write any platform setting; body buffered before size check | writes limited to `cyrus_` keys; oversize refused before reading |
| AC-8 | LOW | Test Flight | `\r` not stripped in `server.properties` values | strip CR, LF, NUL, U+2028/2029/0085 |
| AC-9 | LOW | data packs | a command ending in `\` joins the next entry (1.20.2+) | refused (`line_continuation`) |

| # | Sev | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|

| O-2 | LOW | AI gateway tokens never expire | **closed in r40** (max age) |
| O-3 | LOW | Server Doctor audit-row failures swallowed | open (owner: fail closed or alert) |
| O-4 | LOW | Test Flight log-matcher regexes can backtrack | open (bounded by the runner's kill timeout; RE2 later) |
| O-5 | LOW | pack install/uninstall loop could restart a user's own server about once a minute; in-memory limiter | open (per-server restart budget N/hour is an owner number) |
| O-6 | LOW | no per-user Mod Pack count/byte quota; no create idempotency | open (owner: quota numbers) |
| O-7 | INFO | delivery Idempotency-Key not bound to the body | open (hash body into key) |
| O-8 | LOW | library filters are text-only (no NFKC/confusables, no pixel/audio classifier) | open (hold first-time contributors for review, or a classifier) |
| O-9 | LOW | import licence claim accepted as typed | open (manual review before any public share; public sharing is hard-off) |
| O-10 | INFO | hosted packs are public by sha1 (capability URL, no expiry) | open (owner: OK as public or signed URLs) |
| O-11 | LOW | API v1 replay caches are in-process (50k cap) | open (shared store before more than one instance) |
| O-12 | INFO | the host key is full trust for reads | by design |
| O-13 | - | meshgen kernel-escape untested | open (microVM/gVisor before `CYRUS_MESHGEN_SCRATCH`) |

# 10 Decisions (ADR-style log)

Every owner decision that shapes Cyrus, newest areas last within a group. Format: **ID, date, decision / why / how to apply.** "Owner" = the Nxeon owner. A decision only changes when the owner says so; agents record new ones here (see [14 how to work here](14-how-to-work-here.md)). Parked items are at the end. Open questions that still need an answer are in [12 gaps and roadmap](12-gaps-and-roadmap.md).

## Product and plans
- **D-01, 2026-10-06. Cyrus is a flagship that could stand alone.** Why: differentiator and standalone revenue; the owner wants a "massive asset library" and an easy interface. Apply: build standalone-grade first, plug into Nxeon second; proper research (open source to build on, legal asset sources) before promises; measured Phase 0 spike before claims to customers.
- **D-02, 2026-10-06 / 10-08. Subscription login is acceptable for owner testing only.** Why: a public service cannot run on a subscription. Apply: stay on the subscription until public launch (go-live A3), but switch the build service to an API key with hard spend caps **before any public launch** (runbook step 4).
- **D-03, 2026-10-07. Token economy and plans.** Katara $4.99 / Saka $19.99 / All models $49.99 monthly, stacking, tokens last 3 months; 1 token = $0.002 of real cost; game-server purchases and renewals grant tokens; only games Cyrus builds for earn. Customers never see model family names or per-token USD. Apply: `lib/cyrus/tokens/config.ts` defaults; change via the admin settings.
- **D-04, 2026-10-09. Starter grant = ONE free build** (`cyrus_tok_starter=70`). Free builds without the economy are unmetered, so `cyrus_tok_live` must flip with the studio flag (the launch pair).
- **D-05, 2026-10-10. Plan tiers for assets.** Free and Katara: no studios. Saka: Sound Studio + Sound Library. Top plan (`all`, includes Yakko): everything incl. Texture Studio, Model Studio, Texture Library. **Automatic asset generation follows the user's plan and access** (same gate whether Cyrus, a studio or the library creates the asset). Gates apply to create/edit only; install, keep, rebuild unchanged, export never gated; fail closed on unknown token state.
- **D-06, 2026-10-10. Mod Packs and import-your-own-mod are not plan-gated.** Model use and assets inside them follow tokens and the asset gates.
- **D-07, 2026-10-10. Studios and libraries are top priority**, moved ahead of composition (R1b). The owner's sound library is the Sound Library seed.
- **D-08, 2026-10-10. Config and Stats Studio is foundational** (nobody should need to prompt the AI to change a number). Ungated recommended (editing numbers is not asset creation); the owner has not objected.
- **D-09, 2026-10-10. Motion, animation and effects are foundational and not Minecraft-only.** Vehicles are NOT a Minecraft target; the neutral core must be able to express them; the build waits for the first vehicle-capable game.
- **D-10, 2026-10-10. Defaults the owner accepted unless they say otherwise:** banshee on 1.21.x = custom skin + full sound set on a vanilla-model mob, animated custom-model creatures are 26.x first (BetterModel v3 needs Java 25); generated mods stay on `plugin.yml`; designers, creatures and worldgen come after the foundation; Mod Pack install with open warnings REQUIRES acknowledgement (r29, owner recommendation applied; they may relax it).
- **D-11, 2026-10-08. Launch on 1.21.x, add 26.x right after the usage reset.** Marketing says 1.21.x only until 26.x is buildable.
- **D-12, 2026-10-08. Palworld = Linux only**, no Windows/Wine; Windows-only mods unsupported with an honest reason. tModLoader server variant later; no Docker on the build host; creators must upload art.
- **D-13, 2026-10-08. Loosen Minecraft networking safely.** Capability manifest + host allow-list + anti-SSRF + customer consent + Nxeon AI gateway; default OFF (`cyrus_mod_networking_enabled`).
- **D-14, 2026-10-08. Turn on installing others' published mods at launch** (go-live B8; risk noted: scan gaps and networking off).
- **D-15, 2026-10-11. Hytale, FiveM/RedM and all other games are ON HOLD.** Focus: Minecraft + bridge + cyrus.my + Cyrus + Nxeon at 100%. (Earlier, 2026-10-08: "support ALL games after the usage reset" is superseded.) Hytale research verdict stays conditional GO: needs the Game Server Provider entitlement (each licence authenticates at most 100 servers).

The honest register: what is unverified, what needs the owner, what is not built, and what comes next. Source of truth for status is the tracker `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/CYRUS-TRACKER.md` and owner action lists in `OWNER-ACTIONS.md`; this page is the staff-readable copy and must be updated when they change ([14 how to work here](14-how-to-work-here.md)).

Seven decisions above, staging deploy approval, additive SQL migrations approval (see [reference/db-tables.md](reference/db-tables.md): engine core, managed plugins, catalog v2, library backend, model drafts, telemetry draft, legal cases, notifications, ticket context, API v1, bridge grants), rebuild the image on VM 88001, verify the hardened scan live, API key instead of the subscription login, pack storage + domain, Cloudflare SSL **Full (strict)** + rotate the pasted Cloudflare token + a Nxeon-zone token, DNS/nginx for app/admin/api.cyrus.my, review of 100+ commits before `main`, real-client day, eval budget, legal (ToS licence grant, telemetry wording, content filters, Mojang/platform AI policies).

4. Model Studio next: AI edits inside the studios, an export target for meshes, per-part UV atlas for meshgen output, entry links from the Assets tab, RigSpec v1.1, ItemCuboidSpec.
5. Motion build-out: studio timeline/preview, preset library growth, sound-cue sync, animated textures.
6. Effects/animation asset program (water, doors, effect presets).
7. Community library browse UI + asset-gate wiring; public pass-rate page + evidence badges.
8. Live asset streaming in the build screen.
9. Monorepo extraction day (single agent, alone), then P5 data split cutover, P6 portals, P7 infra move (new servers, R2/CDN, staging, status page, `promote-cyrus.sh` armed), P8 launch gate.
10. Other games as adapters ONLY after the hold lifts, via the onboarding playbook (r47) with a legal review per game.
11. Pre-launch quality list: teams/shared projects, public developer API docs (docs.cyrus.my), marketplace/NxLabs listings and moderation SLAs, DMCA process, per-user AI spend caps, GDPR export/delete, accessibility audit, email deliverability for cyrus.my, load test, disaster-recovery drill, support macros, pricing page truthfulness, `.my` registrant/legal pages.

## Where the details are
`CYRUS-FULL-PLAN.md` (phases P0-P8, bridge, portals, infra), `MASTER-PLAN.md` (engine, R0-R5), `GAPS-AND-IDEAS.md` (red-team findings), `RESEARCH-PLAN.md`, all in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/`.

# 14 How to work here

Rules for anyone (human or agent) changing Cyrus. They come from incidents and owner instructions; see [10 decisions](10-decisions.md) D-50..D-54 and [07 operations](07-operations.md) incident playbooks.

## Worktrees and devhost
- **Never edit or build in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`.** Make your own worktree on the primary: `git -C /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r2 worktree add -b feature/cyrus-rNN-<name> /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-rNN feature/cyrus-r2` (the integration branch is `feature/cyrus-r2`; `main` is production).
- Edit on the primary in your worktree (no `node_modules` there; never symlink one in). Run heavy things on node-2 through `/opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost`: `tsc`, `test [files]`, `build`, `run --lock -- <cmd>`, `dev`, `tunnel`, `pull`, `stop all`, `rm`. **One heavy job at a time** (build lock); agent memory on node-2 is 10 GB. Light, read-only scripts (like the docs generator) can run on the primary with `NODE_PATH=/opt/nxeon/node_modules /opt/nxeon/node_modules/.bin/tsx scripts/cyrus/docs-build.ts`.
- Throwaway DB per worktree on node-2 (`devhost db push|reset|info`). Never use production DB credentials. Forbid role/ownership SQL.
- Commit small and real. **Never `git add -A`** (name paths). Write commit messages to a file and use `git commit -F` (backticks break `-m`). End commits with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- **Never `pkill` by pattern**; stop by systemd unit or port PID.
- Never deploy, migrate production, flip flags, touch VM 88001 or customer servers, or rotate live credentials: the owner does (promote scripts: `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` then `scripts/promote-production.sh`; Cyrus: `scripts/ship`, `promote-cyrus.sh` unarmed).
- No paid third-party spend (baz, model eval runs) without sign-off; no support-ticket replies without sign-off.
- Never write a secret anywhere in the repo or docs; reference where it lives (`/root/.secrets/...`, env files).

## Agent model rules and frugality
Sonnet for research and small items; Opus for big, advanced features, with a tight brief, a report path and caps; few agents; never Fable. Prefer reading existing sources over re-deriving; generate reference pages with scripts (zero model tokens: `scripts/cyrus/docs-build.ts`); one consolidated merge and deploy rather than many small ones.

## How to resume (after a restart or a new session)
1. Read `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/CYRUS-TRACKER.md` (first file after any restart), then [12 gaps and roadmap](12-gaps-and-roadmap.md) and [11 history](11-history.md).
2. `git -C /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r2 log --oneline -20` and `git branch --list 'feature/cyrus-r*'`; for a branch that looks unfinished, `git -C /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-rNN log --oneline` shows which items are committed.
3. Merge latest `feature/cyrus-r2` into your branch before finishing; on a conflict in a generated page, take either side and re-run the generator.
4. For a stopped agent: relaunch for the remaining items only, brief = tracker sections + item list; report to `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/<LETTER>-<name>.md` (under 400 words: what was built, RAN, NOT RUN, owner items).
5. Memory notes (`nxeon-cyrus-*.md`) hold the owner's standing preferences.

## House style for a Cyrus change
Pure core first (schema, validators, simulators, golden files), behind a flag that defaults OFF and fails closed; reach Nxeon only through the host seam; Cyrus tables through `cyrusDb`; plan gates enforced server side; honest limits in customer wording; tests; a real node-2 flight when it touches a server; screenshots (dark, light, phone) looked at; a report with RAN and NOT RUN lists; then the docs checklist below.

## Docs update checklist (the LIVING RULE)
These docs must stay current "for as long as we work on Cyrus". Every merge that changes Cyrus behaviour does the following **in the same branch**:
1. **Regenerate the references:** `npx tsx scripts/cyrus/docs-build.ts` (use `--check` to verify). This updates flags/env/settings, routes, DB tables, version registry, adapters, OpenAPI operations, module map, scripts, tests, the DOCUMENTATION.md index and the feature map. Commit the regenerated `docs/cyrus/reference/*.md`.
2. **Feature map:** a new feature or flag gets a row in `docs/cyrus/_data/features.json` (title, area, flags, doc, branch, state). A new flag with no obvious meaning gets a line in `docs/cyrus/_data/flag-notes.json` (a trailing `*` makes a prefix rule); admin Flags-tab and settings-catalog descriptions are picked up automatically.
3. **Narrative pages:** update the page that owns the change: engine ([02](02-engine.md)), studios ([03](03-studios.md)), assets ([04](04-assets-and-library.md)), bridge ([05](05-bridge-and-accounts.md)), portals ([06](06-portals.md)), operations ([07](07-operations.md)), security ([08](08-security.md)), testing ([09](09-testing-and-verification.md)).
4. **Decision log:** any new owner decision gets an ID in [10](10-decisions.md) (date, why, how to apply); parked items too.
5. **History and gaps:** add the branch/commit to [11](11-history.md) (mark merged vs pending) and move anything newly verified or newly open in [12](12-gaps-and-roadmap.md). Be honest: pending / unmerged / unverified stay marked until proven.
6. **Long form:** the per-feature section in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is still where numbers and proofs go; the Cyrus pages link to it.
7. **Run the gate:** `scripts/devhost test test/cyrus-docs-coverage.test.ts` must pass. It fails when a Cyrus flag / env var / route / table / adapter / version / OpenAPI operation exists in code but not in the generated reference, when generated pages are stale, when `features.json` names a flag or doc that does not exist, and when a relative link in `docs/cyrus` is broken or a page is missing from the README.
8. **Never include:** secrets, the contents of the owner's game-asset archives, or customer data.
Lessons learned after each game onboarding go into the onboarding playbook (r47) and into [10](10-decisions.md).

## Snippet for the repo's agent instructions file
Proposed text for `CLAUDE.md` (not applied by the docs agent so as not to overwrite others' content; the same text is in `docs/cyrus/_data/CLAUDE-SNIPPET.md` for copy-paste):

```
(regenerates docs/cyrus/reference/*), edit docs/cyrus/_data/features.json when a feature or flag is added, update the owning
narrative page and the decision/history/gaps pages, and make test/cyrus-docs-coverage.test.ts pass. Never put secrets or
descriptions of the owner's game-asset archives in docs. See docs/cyrus/14-how-to-work-here.md.
```

## Viewing the docs
Staff-only in the admin: **/admin/docs/cyrus** (renders `docs/cyrus/**` with the same safe Markdown renderer as /admin/docs; requires the `platform` area). In the repo they are plain Markdown; start at [README](README.md).

# Cyrus v8: mod structure (declutter, sub-branches, mod suites)
2026-10-11, branch `feature/cyrus-r45-structure`. Flags: `CYRUS_MOD_SUITES` (off). Mockups: `mock-forge.html`, `mock-suite.html`, `mock-declutter.html` (shots in `shots/`).

## 1. Capability manifest (declutter)
One pure function, `usableFor(game, version, ctx?)` in `lib/cyrus/manifest`, derived only from what already exists: the game adapter (routes, asset delivery, asset profile incl. catalog `accepts`, mesh budget, motion capability), the version registry (capabilities such as `itemModelDefinitions`, `dialogApi`, `animatedCreatures`), the designer feature check (`designFeatures`), `GameSupport` (categories, example prompts) and the plan gate (`canAsset`). Nothing is hand-listed per game.

It returns, for the game and version: studios, asset kinds, routes, designers with their component palettes, library kinds, templates, example prompts, part (module) kinds, and `whyNot` help entries.

**Three states, one rule each:**
| State | When | UI |
|---|---|---|
| usable | the game and version can use it, the plan allows it, the host switch is on | shown |
| locked | usable by the game, blocked only by the PLAN | shown with the lock + upgrade (existing behaviour) |
| hidden | the game or version cannot use it (no route, no delivery, catalog `none`, version capability missing with no fallback), or the host switch is off | not shown; game/version reasons become one `whyNot` line in a small "Why is X not here?" help entry; a switched-off feature gets no line (never leak a flag) |

Examples: Minecraft hides the Mesh studio (no mesh route: `meshBudget` absent, catalog `model: none`), shaders/skies/keybinds/HUD widgets (client-mod route `unsupported`), HDRIs, decals, PBR sets. Minecraft 1.21.1 hides item model states (legacy fallback only), 1.21.1-1.21.6 hide Dialog menus. Terraria, Valheim and Zomboid have no adapter yet: code-only, so every asset studio, designer and asset library kind is hidden and only "describe it" + Files remain (their config exporters are planned), wi

**Applied to:** the studio switch in `StudioShell`, the project page studio list, the library browser and `catalog_search` (kinds the game cannot use are dropped, not shown as locked; per-entry `games[game].fit` stays), the designer palettes (version-only actions/states/layouts), new-mod flow (game, version, category and template pickers), the templates gallery (each template carries `games` + `needs`).

## 2. Sub-branches in the Forge
Selecting a mod pill opens its parts as a second fan beyond the pill (same links, glow and pill anatomy as categories -> mods). Breadcrumb grows one level: Core > Minecraft > Creatures & NPCs > Moth King Saga > Quests: The Moth Pact > Quest designer. Each part node shows its kind icon, a count ("3 items", "48 settings") and a status dot (passed / changed since flight / failed). Click a part: its studio opens scoped to that part (designs filtered to the module; texture/sound studios open on the m

## 3. ModSpec v2: modules
`ModSpecV2 = ModSpecV1 + { schemaVersion: 2, modules[] }`. A module:
`{ id, kind, title, summary?, dependsOn[], requirementIds[], assets[] (slot ids), designs[] (design ids), files[] (owned path prefixes, e.g. custom hooks), provides[] ("item:frost_blade", "entity:moth_king", "quest:moth_pact"), uses[] }`.
Kinds: items, creatures, quests, menus, bosses, hud, textures, sounds, models, motions, config, datapack, worldgen, code.

- **One namespace** (`nx_<8>`): every `provides` id lives under the project's reserved namespace; modules never get their own.
- **Migration v1 -> v2:** a v1 spec becomes ONE module `main` (kind from its route/assets, owns every asset slot and design, requirements all). Lossless; `toV1()` drops modules so v1 consumers keep working. v1 stays the engine default while the flag is off.
- **Cross-reference validation** (structured issues, never throws): duplicate ids, dangling `dependsOn` / asset / design / requirement ids, self-dependency, cycles (with the cycle path), an asset or design owned by two modules, unassigned members (warn), `uses` that no module provides (dangling) or that a module provides but the user does not depend on (missing dependency), foreign namespace. With the design files, references inside designs (`nx_ns:<id>` in quests, bosses, menus, HUDs) are extra

## 4. Scoped edit and build
- `planScopedChange(spec, scope)`: scope = a module or the whole mod. The plan says what the change MAY touch (its designs, slots, owned files, its config keys `items.<id>.*`, `menus.<id>.*`...) and what is read-only context: the INTERFACES of its dependencies (provides lists with one-line signatures) and the uses its dependents make of it (so the edit cannot break them).
- `guardScopedResult(base, ours, theirs, plan)`: a three-way merge per source file. Inside scope: take theirs, unless ours also changed since base (a concurrent manual edit) -> conflict, ours kept, reported. Outside scope: ours always wins and the attempt is reported. Removing a `provides` id a dependent uses is refused unless the scope is the whole mod. Generated outputs (Java from designs, plugin.yml, config.yml layout) are derived and rebuilt, not merged.
- **Revisions:** still one revision chain per project (one jar). Each revision's engine record gains `scope` and `moduleHashes` (content hash per module). A module's revision history is the list of revisions where its hash changed; no new table.
- **Spend:** build tokens are attributed to the revision's scope; per-module spend = sum over its scoped revisions; whole-mod builds show as "whole mod" (never split by guess).
- **Test Flight:** module flight = the module's export (module + dependency closure) built and flown alone; whole flight = the full jar. Status per module: passed / failed / stale (hash changed since the last passing flight) / none.
- **Export a module:** the closure becomes a new v2 spec with a new namespace; ids are rewritten `nx_old:` -> `nx_new:`.

## 5. Decomposed generation (small AI context)
`planSuiteGeneration(spec)`: modules in dependency order; each step gets only its own requirements + dependency interfaces (not their designs). Per-step estimate from the existing estimator. A whole-mod build is the plan run step by step, then one compile, one jar, one whole flight. Not wired to a model on this branch (no paid calls).

## 6. Caps and performance budgets
Single-module mods keep today's limits byte-for-byte. Suites (flag on) get `SUITE_LIMITS`: up to 32 modules, 48 items, 24 menus, 64 quests, 8 bosses, 8 encounters, 4 HUDs, 16 motions, 200 design files. Runtime caps (live bosses, minions, tasks, particles per activation) are plugin-wide and do NOT grow. `suiteBudget()` warns honestly: periodic abilities per player per second, listeners, config settings, generated classes, expected compile time. The thresholds come from a real Test Flight of a lar

## 7. Mod suite vs Mod Pack
| | Mod suite (new) | Mod Pack (exists) |
|---|---|---|
| What | ONE mod built from modules | several separate mods installed together |
| Namespace / jar | one / one | one per mod |
| References | modules reference each other, validated | mods do not know each other |
| Checks | cross-reference + one Test Flight | conflict engine + combined boot |
| UI copy | "Parts of this mod" | "Mods in this pack" |
A module can be exported into its own mod, which can then go into a Mod Pack.

## 8. Risks
- Bigger mods = longer builds and more tokens: per-module estimates first, whole-mod builds show the sum before spending.
- Scope leaks through generated code: only sources of truth are merged; derived files rebuild.
- Interface drift between modules: provides/uses checked on every scoped result.
- Hiding too much: a hidden item always has a `whyNot` line when the reason is the game, never a dead end.

Files: `texture-studio.html`, `sound-studio.html`, `mod-assets.html`, `locked-states.html` (self-contained; sources `src/`, build `tools/build.py`, shots `shots/`).

## Principles
- **Polish in place, no new look.** Tokens, type and chrome are copied from the v5 handoff (`app/dashboard/cyrus/studio.css`): deep space `#05030b`, glass panels, Inter + Space Grotesk + JetBrains Mono, the TopBar crumbs, the conic-rim prompt dock, the inspector tab anatomy, the handoff's 1.7-stroke
- **One accent.** Violet is the only accent. Cyan only means "live": the playhead, the selected layer, the compare splitter. Green, amber and red only mean pass, warn and fail.
- **Truth first.** The mockups run the repo's real code (bundled from `lib/cyrus/textures` and `lib/cyrus/sound`). Quality panels show real `tq-1`/`sq-1` results (the Glock genuinely warns on `palette_size` 49; gunshots warn after peak limiting). Library rows are real manifest metadata. The only sta
- **AI never overwrites**: every Cyrus edit is a candidate to compare, apply in part, or reject.
- **Real light mode**: white glass, inked colours; the portal rail stays a dark island, as in the portal.

## Mapping to backend data
| Screen | Data |
|---|---|
| Texture canvas, layers | `TextureSpec` (generated base, locked) + a raster Paint layer on top. Accepting a candidate swaps the spec. The PNG is a build artifact. |
| Palette, ramps | `spec.palette` (max 24, `MAX_PALETTE`). Ramps are UI groupings; "New ramp" generates 5 hue-shifted shades. |
| Style DNA | The prompt's CUSTOM TEXTURES rules (one outline colour, top-left light, 3-5 shade ramps, no noise or gradients, clear background); compliance is measured with the `noise` and `outline` checks. |
| Checks | `textureQuality()`: `transparency`, `palette_size`, `contrast`, `noise`, `outline`, `vanilla_lookalike` (`not_run`). `soundQuality()`: `format`, `true_peak`, `loudness`, `audible`, `silence_ratio`, `dc_offset`, `duration`, plus a subtitle row. |
| Sound events | `SoundSpec`: sets → events (`role`, `category`, required `subtitle`) → 1-4 weighted variants → up to 4 layers (`lib:` / `synth:` / `silence`, with gain, pitch, start, trim, fades) + processing. The key is `nx_<8>:<set>.<event>`. |
| Meters | `measure()` + `ROLE_PROFILE` bands; auto gain and peak limiting come from `renderVariant()`. |
| Pack status | R0/R1 sync states: hosted, delivery off (`CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL` off), unhosted; `required: false`; the Bedrock line from `assetLines`. |
| Locks | `canAsset(plan, kind, op)`, ported 1:1. Only create/edit is gated. The copy is the gate's own `reason` strings and the `downgradeSpecAssets` notice. |
| History | Asset revisions (spec + render + quality per revision). Restoring makes a new revision. |

- `PixelCanvas({raster, zoom, grid, mirror, backdrop, tool, selection, compare})`, `ToolRail({tool, mirror, grid, color})`, `CompareBar({mode: split|onion|diff|after})`.

- `PaletteStrip({palette, ramps, color, usedCount})`, `RampGenerator({from})`, `StyleDnaStrip({rules, follows})`.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.
